events.title: Wilson Fairchild
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Wilson Fairchild is more than just a country music duo—they’re a force of nature in the industry, known for their unique blend of traditional and contemporary sounds. Comprising cousins Wil and Langdon Reid, Wilson Fairchild brings a rich heritage of music and storytelling to every song they create. With deep roots in the heart of the Shenandoah Valley, their music is a reflection of their upbringing, life experiences, and unwavering love for country music. Wilson Fairchild, the acclaimed duo of Wil and Langdon Reid, continues a musical legacy that spans three generations. Sons of Statler Brothers legends Don Reid and Harold Reid, the cousins proudly carry forward their fathers’ enduring influence on country and gospel music while carving out a sound distinctly their own. As Gaither recording artists, Wilson Fairchild has spent more than 15 years captivating audiences nationwide with their seamless harmonies, quick wit, and heartfelt songwriting. Their performances blend beloved classics with fresh originals, creating an evening filled with laughter, musical excellence, and cherished memories.

events.title: Deconstructing The Music Live! The Dark Side Of The Moon
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: DECONSTRUCTING THE MUSIC LIVE! THE DARK SIDE OF THE MOON A Multimedia Presentation Hosted by Public Television Host SCOTT FREIMAN “Scott’s talk was fascinating! I learned stuff I never knew before – and I was there!” Peter Asher, Grammy-Winning Producer/Artist/Manager and Sirius XM Radio Host In Deconstructing The Music LIVE: Pink Floyd’s The Dark Side of the Moon, Scott Freiman, host of the Public Television series Deconstructing the Beatles, celebrates Pink Floyd’s groundbreaking 1973 album with his first non-Beatles “deconstruction.” Scott will take you on a track-by-track journey through this Pink Floyd masterpiece, explaining the inspiration for the songs and their evolution in the studio. Dark Side of the Moon is a concept album that explores themes of life, death, time, and the human experience. The album features nine tracks that seamlessly flow into each other, creating a cohesive and immersive listening experience. Musically, the album pushed the boundaries of rock music, incorporating elements of jazz, classical, and experimental music.

events.title: Itasca Symphony: Halloween Spooktacular
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Music first, candy after. On Halloween afternoon, the Itasca Symphony Orchestra plays music that has given audiences goosebumps for well over a century, plus the movie and TV themes kids already know by heart. Kids and grown-ups are welcome in costume. The concert is about an hour of music, played by your neighbors in the Itasca Symphony, and it ends in time for trick-or-treating.

events.title: Andreas Klein
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Andreas Klein is widely admired as a pianist of rare sensitivity and musicality. The Washington Post has praised his “articulate and flowing pianism” while the New York Times called him “a pianist who makes silences sound like music.” About a recent Glenn Gould tribute (with the Minguet String Quartet), the Calgary Herald reported, “(Klein brings) to his performance a mature understanding...as well as a brilliant execution”, while Classical Voice of North Carolina (CVNC) was even more blunt: “Andreas Klein is a stupendous pianist...a stunning performance by any standard, and it brought the audience to its feet in a rousing ovation.” He has performed in many of the leading houses of Europe, from Wigmore Hall in London to the Berlin Philharmonie, as well as Carnegie Hall in New York and the Kennedy Center in Washington DC, and is at home with the grandeur of playing with the Berlin Philharmonic or the vast reaches of the Ravinia Festival (where he received two standing ovations) as he is with the intimacy of Le Poisson Rouge (NYC).

events.title: The Seven Wonders A Tribute to Fleetwood Mac
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The Seven Wonders are world-class musicians paying homage to the music of Fleetwood Mac and Stevie Nicks. Named after the Fleetwood Mac song “Seven Wonders,” the band’s collective performing experience brings the crowd powerful renditions of these timeless tunes. They authentically recreate all the great hits of Fleetwood Mac, including Dreams, Go Your Own Way, Rhiannon, Edge of Seventeen, Landslide, Gypsy, and more. The Seven Wonders’ onstage passion reconnects fans with the music they love. Since the Seven Wonders’ inception in 2017, they have garnered national attention for their high energy performances. The Seven Wonders reconnect fans with the music they love. The Seven Wonders’ Teegan Ward commands the stage, channeling the vibrant energy of the youthful prime of Fleetwood Mac’s Stevie Knicks, the driving force behind many of Fleetwood Mac’s most iconic tracks. Ward is the consummate lead on stage, projecting her talent over star-struck audiences. With her world-class voice, incredible presence and high-intensity performance, Ward brings a show that truly inspires.

events.title: Reif Theater Arts Production of Disney’s Aladdin JR.
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Welcome to Agrabah, City of Enchantment, where every beggar has a story and every camel has a tail! Aladdin and his three friends, Babkak, Omar, and Kassim, are down on their luck until Aladdin discovers a magic lamp and the Genie who has the power to grant three wishes. Wanting to earn the respect of the princess, Jasmine, Aladdin embarks on an adventure that will test his will and his moral character. With expanded characters, new songs, and more thrills, this new adaptation of the beloved story will open up “a whole new world” to audiences of all ages! Based on the Tony Award®-winning Broadway musical, audiences’ spirits will soar with excitement over magic, mayhem, flying carpet rides, and songs from the Academy Award®-winning score. Music by Alan Menken Lyrics by Howard Ashman, Tim Rice, Chad Beguelin Book by Chad Beguelin Disney’s Aladdin JR. is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI).

events.title: The Book of Bublé – Christmas
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: “The Book of Bublé – Christmas” is a high-octane holiday tribute to style, swagger, and swing. Emmy® winner Shaun Johnson and his seven-piece band deliver Michael Bublé’s biggest hits with powerhouse vocals and bold new orchestrations—from “Haven’t Met You Yet” to “Feeling Good,” and “Frosty the Snowman” to “It’s Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas.” Drawing on more than two decades of national touring, Shaun, longtime frontman of Tonic Sol-fa and an artist with a recent Top 5 Billboard brings both a vocalist’s and bandleader’s perspective to the repertoire, balancing high-energy performances with the familiar songs that define the season. Musicianship and ensemble work remain at the core, keeping the show fresh and fully in the moment. Backed by a seasoned seven-piece ensemble, The Book of Bublé channels the playful, confident style that earned Shaun multiple Entertainer of the Year nominations – a holiday concert that swings.

events.title: Rock & Roll Xmas Spectacular
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Rock & Roll Xmas Spectacular is a Las Vegas-caliber, multimedia, full-production show that mixes an 8-piece band with music, comedy, parodies and even a game show! Join an all-star cast of musicians as they rock their way through timeless holiday classics and bring new takes on hit songs you didn’t even know were holiday classics. The line-up of musicians is truly legendary as Paul “Stretch” Diethelm and Ted Manderfeld are joined on stage by vocalists Pamela McNeill, Stacy Bauer, and Tim Haussner, and backed by bassist Mike Zeleny, saxophonist and flutist Mike Kreitzer and drummer Billy Thommes. You’ll hear Christmas standards like Silent Night, God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen, Rockin’ Round the Christmas Tree, The Little Drummer Boy and many more like you’ve never heard them performed before! This event is not eligible for any discounts.

events.title: Itasca Symphony: Family Christmas with The Snowman
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The Snowman is back at the Reif with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra for a second December, on its way to becoming a Grand Rapids tradition. The 1982 animated film, based on Raymond Briggs’ picture book, has no dialogue. A boy builds a snowman, the snowman comes to life, and together they fly off into the night sky to “Walking in the Air.” Howard Blake’s music tells the whole story, and the Itasca Symphony Orchestra plays it live while the film fills the big screen. The rest of the afternoon is holiday music for the whole family. Bring the kids and the grandparents, and make it part of your December.

events.title: Reif Cozy Concert: Sarah Morris
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Sarah Morris has a habit of missing the forest. From the day the Minneapolis-based singer-songwriter picked up a guitar, armed with the bone-deep memory of her parents’ well-loved record collection and rooted in the storytelling fire of a Mary Chapin Carpenter tune, she’s been too busy crafting love letters to the details of the trees. Sarah’s endearingly honest, expertly penned songs encourage audiences to pull away from the big picture and get caught up in the magic of our everyday minutia, the rainy day ache in her sunlit voice granting us permission to escape into stories at once hauntingly familiar and uniquely her own.

events.title: Takin’ It to the Limit: An Eagles Tribute with Collective Unconscious and the Fabulous Armadillos
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Now in the 13th incredible year of performing hundreds of sellout performances, The Fabulous Armadillos and Collective Unconscious come together to recreate the magical songs we all know as the premier band of California Rock in the 70’s, known as the Eagles. You will hear all the hits and relive the sound of your turntable spinning all those incredible albums. Hear Take It Easy, Lyin’ Eyes, One Of These Nights, Desperado, I Can’t Tell You Why, Witchy Woman, Hotel California, Take It To The Limit, and so many more! Sit back and close your eyes and bask in the joy of the Eagles live with the Fabulous Armadillos and Collective Unconscious Eagles Tribute – “Takin’ It To The Limit.”

events.title: The Ok Factor
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Olivia Diercks and Karla Peters – cellist and violinist of the new-classical crossover duo, The OK Factor – have one word to describe their musical connection: lucky. The almost telepathic way they respond to one another is palpable to the audiences they capture during performances, as is their spontaneity and joy. Organic and genuine, their original compositions and arrangements feel both comfortingly familiar and uniquely fresh, and have been described as “genre-bending” (Julie Amacher, MPR) and “pure magic” (Wausau Pilot & Review). In their 10+ years of writing, performing, and touring, The OK Factor has honed the ways they impact communities outside the concert hall. Residency work has become a deep passion – sharing intimate performances, conducting outreach activities, and leading workshops for students through their education initiative, ATLAS. Olivia and Karla are also sought-after collaborators and composers-in-residence, having worked with many regional, national, and international artists, and various digital music libraries.

events.title: Itasca Symphony: Sam Miltich with the Itasca Orchestra
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Grand Rapids’ own Sam Miltich joined the Hot Club of San Francisco as a teenager and has since toured internationally and played Lincoln Center. This February he brings his band home to share the Reif stage with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra: Sam on guitar, his father Matthew Miltich on bass, plus other instruments. The music travels. Choro (SHOH-roo) is the quick, bright instrumental music of Rio de Janeiro. The Nuevo Tango from Argentina. Čoček (CHO-chek) is the Romani dance music of the Balkans. And Sam got his start in the swinging guitar jazz Django Reinhardt made famous in 1930s Paris. For the finale, young string players from IOSP’s programs in Grand Rapids, Bigfork, and Remer join the band and the orchestra for one big celebration of music. It’s a February night out of the cold, with musicians of every age on one stage.

events.title: Guys On Ice – An Ice Fishing Musical
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The show follows two lifelong pals, Marvin and Lloyd, as they spend a day in their ice shanty doing everything but catching fish. More than just a play, Guys on Ice is a musical tribute to the stubborn resilience of Midwesterners. Featuring show-stopping numbers like “De Wishing Hole,” “Fish is de Miracle Food,” and the legendary “Ode to a Snowmobile Suit” (featuring a zipper dance routine you have to see to believe), this production captures the heart, the humor, and the “oh-fer-cute” charm of life on the ice.

events.title: Deuces Wild – Dueling Pianos 25th Anniversary Tour
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: There are dueling piano shows...and then there is DEUCES WILD! They are unparalleled in their field and you are in for an incredible night of fun with these two amazing showmen! It is a clap along, sing along musical comedy show where the audience is always a part of the action! No one does it better than Dave and Ted. For a pair of self-taught pianists from Minnesota, David Eichholz and Ted Manderfeld have mastered the sophisticated nuances of burlesque’s best ribald and bawdy traditions. Deuces Wild! Dueling Pianos offers a Las Vegas-style show of comedy and extensive audience participation featuring an unlikely and surprising mix of music and parodies that range from classic rock and country to rap and show tunes. The key to their marathon of musical comedy, however, is the unabashed and completely liberated participation of audience members from 18 to 80. This event is not eligible for any discounts.

events.title: Reif Cozy Concert: Adam Moe
events.description: Adam Moe is a fiddler and singer/songwriter based in Duluth, MN. In 2012, he started the folky-tonk duo Pushing Chain with a former musical partner. For the next eight years, Pushing Chain toured the US and Canada, playing venues big and small and gaining fans the old-fashioned way — face to face, one at a time. Adam has been featured on radio and television, and played some of the biggest festivals in the country, including the 2019 Woody Guthrie Festival and the 2019 Kerrville Folk Festival.

events.title: Reif Theater Arts Presents: Trolls The Musical JR
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Trolls JR. is based on the irreverent DreamWorks Animation movie franchise and features a colorful, wondrous world populated by hilariously unforgettable characters. The show follows the overly optimistic Trolls, constantly with a song on their lips, and the comically pessimistic Bergens, who are only happy when they have Trolls in their stomach. The Troll thespians in Poppy’s company live by their motto: the show must go on. But when a tyrannical foreign emissary arrives in Bergenland, expectations are raised, forcing the Trolls to totally rework their show or risk being served up in the name of diplomacy by a Chef rehired and out for revenge. Based on the DreamWorks Animation Motion Picture In association with Universal Theatrical Group Book & Lyrics by Krista Knight Original Music & Lyrics by Joriah Kwamé Trolls The Musical JR. is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

Based on the DreamWorks Animation Motion Picture In association with Universal Theatrical Group Book & Lyrics by Krista Knight Original Music & Lyrics by Joriah Kwamé Trolls The Musical JR. is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

events.title: Jaerv and OK Factor
events.description: Legendary Swedish group Jaerv and Twin Cities-based duo OK Factor return to the beautiful Sacred Heart alter stage Friday, Oct. 16. The award-winning Jaerv present an extroverted, vigorous and heartfelt folk music with influences from both jazz and pop music. The group offers a varied stage performance where five-voiced tunes blend in with energetic dances and free improvisations. Jaerv is an internationally well known act and has toured the U.S., Japan, Spain, Scotland, Ireland, Finland and Norway among other countries. Their discography includes three full length albums. New classical crossover group OK Factor was formed more than 10 years ago by cellist Olivia Diercks and violinist Karla Peters. Organic and genuine, their original compositions and arrangements feel both comfortingly familiar and uniquely fresh. The group has toured nationally, internationally and recorded five studio albums of original work. Advance E-tickets will be available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Friday, Sept. 11. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only).

events.title: Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold album release concert
events.description: Duluth-based Americana group Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold celebrate the release of their new album “Dedication.” Steeped in musical traditions of folk, bluegrass, country, classic rock, and blues, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold offers a genre-blending sound that is captivating, invigorating, and sure to get your toe tapping. After two decades of writing songs and performing as a solo artist, Danny Frank released of his debut album “Smoky Gold” in 2021. He then assembled an all-star cast of seasoned musicians to fully compliment his music. “The Smoky Gold” is comprised of banjo player Harrison Olk (Tin Can Gin, Cascade Crescendo, Kind Country Band), bassist Joe Scarpellino (Smokin’ Joe, Dead Larry), and fiddle savant Erin Aldridge (Concert Master – Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra). Together the group has recorded and released the full length album “Dedication.” Opening the evening will be Adam Greuel (Horseshoes & Hand Grenades) and Kenny Leiser (Joseph Huber). Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $20 (plus $3.18 in fees) at 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 11 on Eventbrite HERE.

events.title: Silent Film: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
events.description: The Friends of The Felgemaker invite you to experience what it was like to attend a silent movie! Renowned organist Aaron David Miller will accompany the silent film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 on the historic Felgemaker pipe organ housed at Sacred Heart Music Center. Perfect for the Halloween season, “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” is spooky, stylish and historically significant. It is a groundbreaking German horror film which set standards for creative camera work and featured a dark and twisted style of storytelling. It is widely considered the first true horror story put to film. This masterpiece influenced later film directors such as Alfred Hitchcock and Tim Burton. Attendees are encouraged to come dressed for Halloween, adding to the film’s haunted atmosphere. Aaron David Miller returns to Sacred Heart Music Center to accompany this film on the Center’s outstanding Felgemaker pipe organ. Miller is noted for his highly imaginative and creative style, found in his performances, improvisations and compositions. He has won numerous international awards for improvisation and has given concerts and accompanied silent films across the country.

events.description: Duluth artists celebrate the 20th anniversary of My Chemical Romance’s classic album “The Black Parade.” Considered an emo rock masterpiece, the concept album “The Black Parade” is a career defining work from American rock band My Chemical Romance. The full album will be performed by an all-star Duluth band featuring members from Jumpsuit, Between Howls, Gemstones, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold, The Draco Volans, Duluth Transit Authority, and many more. Duluth-based Ephemera opens. Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $15 (plus $2.85 in fees) at 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 11 on Eventbrite HERE. events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Minnesota troubadour Mason Jennings returns performing old favorites and work from his new album “Dark Wings.” “I love song craft,” says Mason Jennings, a folksinger who has spent over two decades honing his craft both on stage and in the studio. “A song is like a boat on the water, and you’re trying to make it float with as few pieces as possible. If you do it right, a song can be very healing.” For Jennings, songwriting has always been about a personal connection, both with his audience and himself. He’s known for an unpretentious, emotive approach to folk music, combining introspective lyrics with acoustic melodies. His work has drawn comparisons to genre greats, including Nick Drake, John Fahey, and Tom Waits. But Jennings’ sound is distinctly his own, one that blends vulnerability with strength, simplicity with complexity. That style comes through on his new record: “Dark Wings.” His 18th studio album, the record finds Jennings moving between raw honesty about childhood scars, dark thoughts, spiritual questioning and a stubborn belief in the power of love.

events.title: Iron Range Night
events.description: The Iron Range Rocks! Celebrate the music from Minnesota’s Iron Range with performances from The Brothers Burn Mountain, Hobo Revival and The Sectionals beginning at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28. Guitar and drum duo Ryan and Jesse Dermody have been performing as The Brothers Burn Mountain for 25 years. Based out of their off-the-grid, self-constructed studio near Cotton, the duo has toured relentlessly around the midwest for more than two decades. The Brothers Burn Mountain have released 11 full-length albums of original music and released a “best of” collection in 2025. Hobo Revival, based out of Nashauk, has been performing their straight-ahead brand of rock and roll across northern Minnesota for 15 years. Led by singer-songwriter Kim Nagler, the group released its latest album “The Pulled Pork Sessions” in 2024. The Sectionals are a vocal octet performing classic jazz and modern acapella favorites. The ensemble features members from throughout the Iron Range. This event is made possible in part by a grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council with funds appropriated from the Minnesota Legislature from its General Fund.

events.description: The New Standards Holiday Show has wowed Twin Cities audiences for years. The group will bring its merriment machine to the Sacred Heart Music Center altar stage for the first time at 7:30 pm Thursday, Dec. 10. The New Standards Holiday Show features the trio as wise-cracking hosts of a freewheeling variety spectacle. They’re joined by a cavalcade of instrumentalists and guests in what has become an enduring, and endearing, Minnesota holiday tradition. events.description: Celebrate the holidays bluegrass-style. Minnesota bluegrass songstress Becky Schlegel performs Christmas classics with The High 48s at 7 pm Saturday Dec. 12. With a voice that floats, whispers, and soars, Becky Schlegel is a songwriter whose music bridges country, bluegrass, and folk traditions providing a wonderful foundation for so many holiday favorites. Becky will be joined on stage by the High 48s Since forming in northeast Minneapolis in 2006, The High 48s have been making music that combines the soulful sound of classic bluegrass with a modern attitude. Opening the show will be Duluth duo Salt and Pine. Don’t miss this special holiday concert on our beautiful altar stage. events.description: Minneapolis-based The Last Revel brings its exciting Americana-folk sound to the beautiful Sacred Heart altar stage at 7:30 pm Thursday, Jan. 14. Formed in 2011, The Last Revel uses traditional folk-minded three part harmonies with honest and meaningful lyrics to deliver a passionate and soul stirring performance. events.title: World Ballet Company: Swan Lake
events.description: Here Make it a group experience! Special pricing is available for groups of 10 or more: worldballetcompany.com/group-tickets. The World’s MOST Iconic Ballet – With a LIVE Orchestra! The legendary tale of Swan Lake takes flight in a breathtaking production from World Ballet Company, as fate and magic entwine in a timeless battle between good and evil. Performing with a Live Orchestra, and featuring a cast of 50 international dancers, over 150 radiant hand-sewn costumes, and stunning hand-crafted sets, this spellbinding ballet captures every heart-pounding moment – from the Dance of the Little Swans to the Black Swan’s 32 fouettés, and every pirouette in between. With Tchaikovsky’s unforgettable score soaring through the air and played LIVE, immerse yourself in this mesmerizing journey where dreams, heartbreak, and hope unfold right before your eyes. events.title: Duluth Haunted Ship 2026
events.description: Welcome to the home of the William A. Irvin Haunted Ship Tours in Duluth, Minnesota! That hint of cool breeze you feel isn’t just a change of weather. Those are the spirits of the Duluth Haunted Ship swinging on anchor just outside your view. The ghouls on board are waiting to morph the William A. Irvin historic freighter into something truly sinister. This season marks the 31st year of this unhallowed event, starting Friday, October 2, 2026 and running long weekends through Halloween (plus MEA Wednesday, October 14, 2026). This year, you can look forward to more activity outside of the ship on Harbor Drive: enjoy food trucks every Friday & Saturday, lights, bonfires, drinks available for purchase, and more. Avoid the General Admission (GA) line and buy a FAST PASS ticket. Enter through FAST PASS gate. General Admission tickets enter through the GA line. All tickets are valid for one tour. You may arrive anytime during open hours for the date that your ticket is valid. Tickets can be purchased at the gate. No child under the age of 12 will be admitted without a caregiver. The ship is not handicapped accessible. All sales are final. No refunds.

events.description: Ride the Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad. A historic 2-hour rail journey through the majestic St. Louis River Estuary. Family-friendly, volunteer-run, and purely Duluth. events.title: Hadestown
events.description: Hadestown, previously scheduled for March 16, 2026, at the DECC Symphony Hall, has been POSTPONED due to travel conditions and restrictions surrounding the Midwest Winter Storm. The performance has been rescheduled for Monday, October 19, 2026. All current tickets will be valid for the October performance. COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society.

events.title: History Happy Hour
events.description: Step into the 1920s for an evening of cocktails, hors d’oeuvres, music, and history at Glensheen! Begin your evening by entering through the Juliet Balcony, where you’ll be greeted with a cocktail and hors d’oeuvres before heading downstairs to explore Glensheen’s basement. Discover 1920s-inspired activities and artifacts on display, enjoy music from the era, snap a photo in the billiards room, and take in a few surprises along the way. Enjoy a selection of fun, 1920s-inspired cocktails available for purchase at the cash bar before settling in for an engaging history talk by local historian Tony Dierckins. Tony will present “Drying Out Duluth: From Temperance to Prohibition,” exploring Duluth’s complicated relationship with alcohol—from the city’s early liquor ordinances and temperance movement to Prohibition and the creative ways Duluthians continued to enjoy a drink. Following the talk, enjoy dessert and a special 1920s-themed experience to round out the evening. Dress to impress and embrace the spirit of the 1920s for this one-of-a-kind night at Glensheen. This event is for guests ages 21 and older. Doors open at 5:30 p.m. | Talk begins at 6:30 p.m. | Event ends at 9 p.m.

events.title: Whoopsa Daisy Farm
events.description: Come and explore the farm with your family. Jump in the corn pit, dig in the sandbox, or explore Dinoland and Fairyland. There are two playgrounds, yard games, a wagon ride through the Whimsical Woods and so much more. Feed the donkeys, goats, and chickens and walk through the berries. The farm is open to everyone Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, August 7 through October 25, 2026, from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. We will also open Thursday, October 15 for MEA weekend from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. Tickets are sold at the entrance in the yellow building. The cost is $8.00 a person, and infants are free. Everything on the farm is included in the price. We are off Highway 53 in Duluth at 5399 Samuelson Road.

events.title: Duluth Haunted Ship 2026
events.description: Welcome to the home of the William A. Irvin Haunted Ship Tours in Duluth, Minnesota! That hint of cool breeze you feel isn’t just a change of weather. Those are the spirits of the Duluth Haunted Ship swinging on anchor just outside your view. The ghouls on board are waiting to morph the William A. Irvin historic freighter into something truly sinister. This season marks the 31st year of this unhallowed event, starting Friday, October 2, 2026 and running long weekends through Halloween (plus MEA Wednesday, October 14, 2026). This year, you can look forward to more activity outside of the ship on Harbor Drive: enjoy food trucks every Friday & Saturday, lights, bonfires, drinks available for purchase, and more. Avoid the General Admission (GA) line and buy a FAST PASS ticket. Enter through FAST PASS gate. General Admission tickets enter through the GA line. All tickets are valid for one tour. You may arrive anytime during open hours for the date that your ticket is valid. Tickets can be purchased at the gate. No child under the age of 12 will be admitted without a caregiver. The ship is not handicapped accessible. All sales are final. No refunds.

events.title: Glensheen Lantern Tours
events.description: Experience illuminated history, a tour of the mansion lit only by lantern light. Led by expert tour guides, Lantern Tours are a favorite during the Halloween season. This tour is well suited for guests who have previously experienced the Classic or Full Mansion Tours. Available Fridays & Saturdays in October.

events.title: Neighborhood 3: Requisition of Doom
events.description: Something strange is happening in the suburbs. Parents are stunned when their kids become addicted to an online horror video game. The setting? A neighborhood of identical houses. The goal? Smash through an army of zombies to escape. But when the game starts bleeding into reality, both parents and players discover that fear has a life of its own. Written by Jennifer Haley (Hemlock Grove, Mindhunter), this darkly funny, wildly creepy play delivers an unforgettable theatrical ride with “an affectingly gruesome finale” (Variety).

events.title: Sierra Duluth Grand Opening
events.description: Sierra, part of the TJX family of brands (TJ Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods, Homesense), is opening its doors in Duluth on Saturday, October 24 at 8 a.m. at Burning Tree Plaza (5115 Burning Tree Road). The +17,000 sq. ft. store will carry top-brand apparel, footwear, and gear for hiking, running, everyday movement, and everything in between — all at 20–60% off department and specialty store prices. Sierra’s mission resonates locally — whether shoppers are hiking along the Superior Hiking Trail or jogging the Lakewalk along Lake Superior, there’s something for every level of adventurer. Some further details: • Grand Opening Day: The grand opening will feature a ribbon cutting, Sierra-branded giveaways, and a hidden hang-tag activity featuring gift cards hidden throughout the store. • Local Hiring: The store is actively hiring full- and part-time associates! We’d love to have you join us!

events.title: High Key Mondays & Industry Nights
events.description: High Key Mondays & Industry Night Are BACK! Live local music | Drink specials | 6–9pm High Key Monday is FRI-YAY for many of our industry partners — and we’re roll with it. Calling all restaurant, bar, liquor store, and brewery professionals in the Twin Ports — get on down to the Paddle for Industry Night! Show a worker ID or pay stub for $1 off all Bent Paddle beverages. Thank you for keeping our paddles in the water! Everyone is welcome! Come for the tunes, stay for the conversations, delicious beverages, and good times. This month to kick off and celebrate the return, we invite you to connect with local organizations making waves in the Twin Ports — like WE Health, Trans+ Northland, Twin Ports Artists Collective, and Men As Peacemakers. Org’s may vary based on who available each week, but the good vibes are guaranteed!

events.title: Daniel In The Lions’ Den – Duluth
events.description: Get ready for an unforgettable night at the Gas South Theater in Duluth, Georgia, as we present “”Daniel In The Lions’ Den – Duluth.”” This captivating musical brings to life the timeless story of courage and faith, set against a backdrop of stunning performances and vibrant storytelling. The atmosphere at the Gas South Theater is electric, making it the perfect venue to experience this powerful tale that resonates with audiences of all ages. Join us for an evening filled with inspiration and entertainment, as talented performers take the stage to share Daniel’s incredible journey. Whether you’re a theatre enthusiast or looking for a family-friendly outing, “”Daniel In The Lions’ Den – Duluth”” promises to be a highlight of your season. Don’t miss out on this enchanting experience—secure your tickets now and be part of the magic!

events.title: Zach Williams
events.description: With Cochren & Co. and Christian Hohn Revival Nights 2026 – Presented by Awakening Events Tickets on sale now! The Zach Williams Tour 2026 is bringing an energy this fall that’s a little gritty, a lot louder, and always real. Performing in 21 cities across the country, these shows weave together the perfect blend of country, rock, and a gospel message. Zach Williams brings the power behind “Chain Breaker” and “Rescue Story” while Cochren & Co. make waves with their favorites like “Church (Take Me Back)” and “Running Home.” Singer/Songwriter Christian Hohn opens the night with new music that tells his story of faith in way that suits this tour’s theme of everyday life, struggle, and redemption. It’s the kind of night you don’t want to miss! A limited number of VIP tickets offer best seating, early merch shopping, and a Meet & Greet with photo opportunity with Zach Williams. Grab your seats before they’re gone!

events.title: Art Night Out: Materials and Self with Andrew Webster, Robb Quisling, and Lauren Faherty
events.address: 130 W. Superior St, Suite 400, Duluth, MN
events.description: Three artists, one theme: explore Materials and Self at this Art Night Out featuring an artist talk with reclaimed materials artist Andrew Webster, found object painter Robb Quisling, and fiber artist Lauren Faherty. Each artist brings a personal perspective to the question of how materials and objects tie into our lives, carry our stories, and intersect with creative practice. Enjoy snacks, beverages, and the three exhibitions on view starting October 19.

events.title: Neural Exercises for Autism, a conversation with the author
events.venue: At Sara’s Table Chester Creek Cafe
events.description: Is Autism an identity or a disorder, is an ongoing question which faces those who describe themselves under the umbrella of Neurodiversity language. WW Norton author, and autistic individual, Sean Inderbitzen LCSW, DSW, invites neurodiverse Duluthians to wrestle with this question with him in a small gathering setting. Themes to be covered from his new book in this talk include identity, temperment, disorder, empathy, and the role of ambiguous loss in shaping connection and rigidity. These themes like these and more appear in his new book Neural Exercises for Autism, and we invite you to meet with the author partaking in discussion, pastries, and a dive into meaning and neurodiversity. Please register for our gathering complete with readings, discussion, pastries from Sara’s Table at Chester Creek Cafe, and Alcoholic beverages available for purchase. Pastries will be provided for those who wish to partake, and beverages are guest responsibility. Our event is on a first come first serve basis. If you are unable to make it and register, please cancel as space is limited to the first 25 registrations.

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: With special guest Goldy LockS Band Thursday, November 5, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment Tickets on sale now! ABOUT 38 SPECIAL Formed in 1974, the band toured tirelessly from the start, sharpening the explosive live show that’s been 38 Special’s calling card for a half-century. Along the way, the Florida natives fine-tuned their sound too: a blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks that would soon become staples of FM radio. Years passed... trends changed... some band members retired from the rigors... but 38 Special remained, hitting the road year after year, flying the flag for an enduring form of classic rock & roll that never dies. As 38 Special enters its sixth decade together, the music continues with Milestone. It’s the band’s first studio album in more than 20 years, and it showcases a group of road warriors with plenty of miles left in the tank. Fueled up on snarling guitars, anthemic melodies, and the desire to break new ground, they update their sound for the 2020s, bridging the gap between past and present without forgetting their rock & roll roots.

events.title: Gary Owen
events.description: No Hard Feelings Tour Tickets on Sale Now! ABOUT GARY OWEN Gary Owen has been entertaining audiences for more than two decades with his sharp observational humor and fearless storytelling. Known for his unapologetic, rule-defying style, his material draws from his personal life, time in the military and the everyday absurdities that connect people across backgrounds. With a fanbase that has grown by the millions in recent months and continues to surge across social media, Owen’s reach has cemented his place as one of the most in-demand touring comedians today. Beyond stand-up, Owen has appeared in a wide range of feature films including BACK ON THE STRIP with Tiffany Haddish and Wesley Snipes, MEET THE BLACKS and its sequel THE HOUSE NEXT DOOR, THINK LIKE A MAN and THINK LIKE A MAN TOO, RIDE ALONG with Ice Cube and Kevin Hart, LITTLE MAN opposite the Wayans Brothers, and DADDY DAY CARE with Eddie Murphy. He is also widely recognized for his scene-stealing role as “Bearcat” in the MGM film COLLEGE. On television, Owen starred in his own BET series THE GARY OWEN SHOW and co-hosted TruTV’s sketch series UPLOAD WITH SHAQUILLE O’NEAL.

events.title: An Evening With Neil deGrasse Tyson
events.description: An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I Presented by Roberts Group Tickets on sale now! “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. The final report was published in 2002 and contained recommendations (for Congress and for the major agencies of the government) that would promote a thriving future of transportation, space exploration, and national security.

events.title: Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance.

events.title: The Oak Ridge Boys
events.description: Friday, November 13, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment HERE ABOUT THE OAK RIDGE BOYS For more than 50 years, The Oak Ridge Boys have defined one of the most recognizable sounds in American music, blending four-part harmonies with an energetic stage presence that has earned them Grammy, CMA, ACM, and Dove Awards. With a legacy that stretches from their Gospel roots in the 1940s to their rise as Country‐Pop hitmakers, the group—Duane Allen, Joe Bonsall, William Lee Golden, and Richard Sterban—has delivered classics like Elvira, Bobbie Sue, American Made, and Thank God for Kids. Their music has produced multiple gold and platinum albums, over 30 Top Ten hits, and collaborations with icons ranging from Johnny Cash and Paul Simon to George Jones and Ray Charles. Today’s performing members are Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Richard Sterban, and Ben James. The Oak Ridge Boys remain one of the most enduring and dynamic touring acts in the world, known for a high‐energy show that celebrates both their rich history and their continued evolution.

events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society.

events.venue: 199 Alger Smith Rd, Knife River, MN 55609, United States
events.address: 199 Alger Smith Rd, Knife River, MN
events.description: 🎄 JULEBYEN 2026 – Scandinavian Nordic Christmas Village Festival 🎄 Step into the magic of a Nordic Christmas at Julebyen 2026, a one-of-a-kind holiday festival celebrating the traditions, culture, and festive spirit of Scandinavia! events.title: Creepmas Parade Duluth
events.description: The Creepmas Parade is an annual outdoor costume parade focused on folklore, blending Krampusnacht traditions and Creepmas aesthetics. Participants are encouraged to respectfully dress up as winter myths, cryptids or any creature that resonates with them. Bells are the unifying piece of the parade and organizers encourage everyone to jingle and jangle along the parade route. The parade takes place on the first Saturday in December. The parade can be joined at any point along the route.

events.title: A Christmas Story – Duluth

Join us for an unforgettable evening filled with catchy tunes and delightful performances that will leave you humming long after the curtain falls. Whether you’re a lifelong fan or new to the story, “”A Christmas Story – Duluth”” promises to be a magical experience that will warm your heart this holiday season. Don’t miss out on this festive celebration—book your tickets now and make memories that will last a lifetime!

events.description: Presented by Pepper Entertainment Tuesday, February 16, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm ON SALE NOW ABOUT DAUGHTRY Formed in 2006, the Grammy Award®- nominated, multi-platinum rock band Daughtry has remained a dominant force for nearly two decades. events.title: DSSO Masterworks 5 – In Sacred Light
events.description: A kaleidoscope of perspectives: “My Country ‘Tis of Thee”, filtered through Charles Ives’ shifting lenses. Fragments of a brilliant Schubert symphony left mysteriously unfinished. An old Lutheran hymn refracted and retold by Bach. A journey from light to darkness and back again, pieced together from a mosaic of sacred texts. Tonight’s program represents the American ideal of individual voices converging into one, unified whole. Featuring the DSSO Chorus and DSSYO Youth Symphony IVES Variations on “America” SCHUBERT Symphony No. 8, “Unfinished” BACH Cantata No.

events.title: NEEDTOBREATHE with special guest Conner Smith
events.description: Presented by Pepper Entertainment Sunday, February 21, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm ON SALE NOW ABOUT NEEDTOBREATHE NEEDTOBREATHE is known for their distinctive blend of Americana, alt-rock, and spiritual depth—earning five No. 1 albums, over three billion career streams, sold-out tours, and a devoted global following. The South Carolina–bred group—Bear Rinehart, Josh Lovelace, Tyler Burkum, and Randall Harris—enters a new creative chapter with The Long Surrender, their tenth studio album and first release for MCA. Produced by nine-time GRAMMY-winner Dave Cobb, The Long Surrender captures the band at their most vulnerable and instinctive, recorded largely live and driven by Rinehart’s deeply personal songwriting. Led by the early standout “Momma Loves Me” featuring The Red Clay Strays, the album reflects themes of faith, redemption, and renewed clarity—showcasing a band confident enough to strip everything back and let the songs speak for themselves. “This album really clarified that, as an artist, I’ve got to put my convictions in front of anything else,” says Rinehart.

events.title: Riverdance 30 – The New Generation
events.description: Sunday, March 14, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Roberts Group Tickets on sale now! Since Riverdance first emerged onto the world stage, its fusion of Irish and international dance and music has captured the hearts of millions worldwide. The Grammy award-winning music and the infectious energy of its mesmerizing choreography and breathtaking performances has left audiences in awe and established Riverdance as a global cultural sensation. To celebrate this incredible 30th year milestone, Riverdance will embark on a special anniversary tour, bringing its magic to audiences around the world. This spectacular production rejuvenates the much-loved original show with new innovative choreography and costumes and state of the art lighting, projection and motion graphics. And for the first time Riverdance welcomes “The New Generation” of performers, all of whom were not born when show began 30 years ago. John McColgan, Director of Riverdance said, “For over 30 years, Riverdance has taken us on a unique and exhilarating journey with the love and support of our audiences. The show has developed from a stage spectacle into a global cultural phenomenon.

events.title: Flashlight Tours of Fairlawn Mansion
events.description: Celebrate Spooky Season by taking a tour of Fairlawn Mansion after dark! This special guided tour takes place in the dark by lantern light. Our superstition experts will share Victorian superstitions, haunted history, and even their own paranormal experiences! This 30-minute tour takes you throughout all three floors of Fairlawn Mansion. You will see traditional Victorian era funeral and mourning decor, photographs, and even some artifacts from our own experiences of unexplained activity inside Fairlawn! 30 Minute tours starting at 6:30pm with the last tour departing at 9:30pm. Admission is $10/person. Tickets may be purchased at www.superiorhistoricproperties.org. Wear your Halloween costume for an even spookier experience! No full-face masks or inflatable costumes allowed and weapons are prohibited. There is no elevator at Fairlawn Mansion, so plan to wear comfortable shoes to climb stairs.

events.title: Ghost in the Gallery
events.venue: Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center
events.description: Ghosts in the Bong Center Museum Galleries! This Halloween season, the Bong Veterans Museum invites you to experience our museum in a whole new light. On October 24th, you can alter your vision and get spooky if you choose. The galleries will take on a mysterious atmosphere; visitors of all ages are welcome to wander through exhibits where history and imagination blur. Our mannequins have always stood watch, but during this special event you may find yourself asking—are they moving, or is it just the season playing tricks on you?Families can enjoy a mild, sensory-friendly adventure designed to spark curiosity without ever overwhelming younger visitors. For those who prefer a gentler experience, accommodations will be made to ensure everyone can participate at their own comfort level.This isn’t a haunted house—it’s a chance to celebrate the spooky season in a unique, educational, and welcoming environment. Discover the secrets of our mannequins, share in the fun of Halloween with your loved ones, and see the Bong Center like you’ve never seen it before. Regular admission applies.

events.title: Echoes of Elegance: English Renaissance
events.description: Step back in time for an unforgettable afternoon of music at Fairlawn Mansion. Join us for a classical concert performed on beautifully preserved historical instruments, bringing the rich, resonant sounds of the past to life within the Mansion’s elegant surroundings. Lutenists Edward Martin and Phillip Rukavina are presenting a concert: "English Renaissance Lute Duets from the Elizabethan and Jacobean eras". Music from this period is fresh, tuneful and engaging, featuring delightful pieces by Downland, Danyel, Lawes, Pilkington, Sampson, Johnson, Robison, and Allison. These duets are audience favorites. Martin and Rukavina have recorded extensively, are teachers, and have performed throughout the USA and Europe. Tickets may be purchased online at: www.superiorhistoricproperties.org.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.venue: Virtual on Zoom: Register at uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor to receive the Zoom link.
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance.

events.title: Ely For Ely: Community Legacy & Transfer of Wealth
events.description: A significant amount of wealth is expected to transfer to Ely over the next 10-20 years, creating opportunities for community endowments, charitable giving, and legacy investments. This series of Ely for Ely gatherings will explore the scale of opportunity Ely has to embrace its huge reach to create lasting wealth for future generations. Together, we will learn more about estate planning, charitable tools, local giving pathways, and more. These meetings are open to all. Boundary Waters Connect facilitates an Ely for Ely planning committee, made up of local nonprofit leaders, business owners, and community members, to host a monthly networking and professional development program for Ely-area entrepreneurs, nonprofit leaders, and community members interested in making positive contributions to local affairs. The first meeting in each series will frame the conversation; the second will be an in-depth look at the track, maximizing Extension research, insights, and data. The Minnesota Secure Choice Retirement Program will discuss the requirements for Minnesota employers under state statute. This will include the compliance and rollout timelines, employer responsibilities, and a breakdown of the Program benefits for Minnesota workers and employers. events.title: Photo Submission Contest – 2027 Area Directory
events.description: We’re looking for stunning outdoor photos that capture the beauty, culture, and spirit of Itasca County! Submit your best vertical (portrait orientation) shots for a chance to be featured in our 2027 Grand Rapids Area Directory and win Chamber Bucks to be used at any Chamber member business! Prizes 1st Place: $250 in Chamber Bucks + Photo featured on the cover of the 2027 Grand Rapids Area Directory Photos used inside the Directory: $25 in Chamber Bucks + Photo featured inside the Directory Photo Submission Guidelines Orientation: Photos must be portrait (vertical) to fit the Directory cover layout. Location: All photos must be taken outdoors in Itasca County, MN. Content: Highlight scenic landscapes, seasonal beauty, outdoor recreation, our culture, or local landmarks. People may be included but avoid close-ups. Image Quality: High-resolution photos (300 DPI minimum) preferred; smartphone photos accepted if they meet quality standards. Branding: No visible brand names, logos, or watermarks. If a selected photo contains brand logos, they will be digitally removed. Original Work: You must be the original photographer and hold full rights to the image.

Serving on the Chamber Board is an opportunity to bring your perspective to the table, help guide the priorities and direction of the organization, and be part of conversations that impact businesses throughout our area. Why Serve? As a Chamber Board member, you will have the opportunity to: • Help shape Chamber priorities, programs, and advocacy efforts. • Represent the perspectives and needs of our business community. • Build relationships with business and community leaders. • Contribute your experience, ideas, and perspective to the Chamber’s future. • Help strengthen the business environment in the Grand Rapids area. events.title: Blend your Bliss | Essential Oil Class
events.description: Step into the aromatic world of essential oils and discover how scent can support wellness, mood, and daily ritual. In this beginner-friendly workshop, you'll learn the foundations of aromatherapy, including the history of essential oils, how they're made, safe and effective use, and the unique characteristics of top, middle, and base notes. Through guided exploration and hands-on blending, you'll gain confidence in choosing oils that resonate with your needs and intentions. Courtney will share practical blending tips, favorite recipes, and support you in creating a custom aromatherapy roll-on to take home. Whether you're brand new to essential oils or looking to deepen your understanding, you'll leave with both knowledge and a personalized botanical blend crafted by your own hands. Taught by Courtney Olby All supplies included. No experience necessary.

events.title: Book Group with MPR's Kerri Miller
events.description: Kerri Miller, host of MPR's Talking Volumes, will be leading a discussion of Peace Like a River by Leif Enger The public is invited. Kerri Miller is the host of MPR's Big Books & Bold Ideas, a Friday podcast and show all about books. She is also operates Siren Sojourns, leading adventure travel for adventurous readers. On this particular weekend, she's leading a Bayfield Book Retreat. "Peace Like a River serves as a reminder of why we read fiction to begin with.” said the San Francisco Chronicle when it was published more than twenty years ago. And we couldn't agree more.

events.title: Crafting Traditional Soap
events.description: Friday November 13th 2026, 5:30pm - 7pm Step into the timeless craft of soap making with artisan soap maker Lindsay Larson. In this class, you’ll be guided through the complete process of creating handcrafted soap using reclaimed animal fat; a sustainable, traditional ingredient once used in every homestead kitchen. Together, we’ll explore the alchemy of transforming rendered fat, lye, and botanicals into a cleansing, nourishing bar of soap. You’ll learn about safety practices, temperature control, ingredient selection, and mold preparation, along with tips on sourcing high-quality materials and natural additives. This is a guided learning experience, perfect for anyone curious about the old ways of soap making and eager to bring this lost art back into their own home practice. Consider bringing: A notebook and writing utensil You Receive: Step by step notes on soap making, one bar of the soap made in class.

events.title: Indigenous History Around Lake Superior: Why It Matters Today

The bar will be open, serving drinks, Lyla's Pizzas (we have a pizza oven), snacks, and Fat Radish sandwiches. $5 suggested donation at the door.

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: City Council Meeting
events.description: In-Person Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meetings are open to the public and held in council chambers at the Proctor Area Community Center (PACC) 100 Pionk Drive Proctor, MN. Public comments may also be submitted in advance of the meeting to cityhall@proctormn.gov up to 3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting with the e-mail title “City Council Meeting.”

events.title: National First Responder Day
events.description: National First Responders Day on October 28 recognizes the heroic men and women who make it their business to take immediate action when disaster strikes. Not sure what a first responder does? Just think about 9/11 for a moment. Firefighters, police, paramedics, and more — rushing into Lower Manhattan. Whether you’ve had your own emergency or not, it’s not hard to understand and appreciate the dangerous and difficult work they do.

events.title: Retail Employee Day
events.description: Today the City of Proctor proudly recognizes the hardworking team at Mountain Spirits Municipal Liquor Store in honor of Retail Employees’ Day. Retail Employees’ Day celebrates the dedicated people who keep stores running and ensure customers have a positive shopping experience. From helping customers find the perfect bottle, stocking shelves, managing inventory, and keeping the store welcoming and organized, retail employees play an important role in connecting products with the people who enjoy them. At Mountain Spirits, our team works year-round to provide friendly service, maintain a well-stocked store, and support this City or Proctor’s municipal enterprises. Their efforts help make shopping easy, enjoyable, and welcoming for everyone who walks through the door. Please join us in thanking the Mountain Spirits staff for their hard work, professionalism, and commitment to serving the Proctor community. Your dedication does not go unnoticed!

events.title: General Election
events.description: 2026 GENERAL ELECTION NOTICE The 2026 State General Election will be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places will be open from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Voters who are in line by 8:00 PM are still eligible to vote. Absentee voting for the General Election began on September 18, 2026. Minnesota voters may vote by mail or in person before Election Day. Residents can use the Minnesota Secretary of State’s website to: Find their polling location Register to vote View a sample ballot Request an absentee ballot Track an absentee ballot Minnesota Votes - Election Information Minnesota also allows eligible voters to register or update their voter registration at their polling place on Election Day. For additional election information, please contact the City Clerk at (218) 749-3579 or visit the Minnesota Secretary of State’s website.

events.description: PUBLIC HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES BOARD The Human Services Board includes the 5 county commissioners and the chairs of the PHHS Advisory Committee and Local Mental Health Advisory Committee. The board has authority to administer all public health and human services programs. Some of the Board’s specific functions are: set policy; appropriate funds and approve expenditures, monitor agency progress toward outcomes; assure adequate staffing for program delivery and advocate for changes to meet the needs of the local community.

events.title: Celebrity Dance Challenge
events.description: 2026 marks the 20th Anniversary of Minnesota Ballet’s Celebrity Dance Challenge, an annual fundraising event that pairs local celebrities with professional dancers from the company for a fun and competitive evening of dance. Participants perform in a range of styles—such as ballroom, jazz, and contemporary—and audience members vote for their favorites. The event includes a social hour, refreshments, and a high-energy show. Social hour with appetizers and cash bar starts at 5:30; performance at 7:00 pm in the Depot Theatre. Proceeds from the Celebrity Dance Challenge support the Minnesota Ballet’s educational programs and its professional dance company, helping sustain its mission of artistic excellence and community engagement.

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
events.description: Karl von Rabenau’s original choreography transforms Washington Irving’s legendary ghost story into the ultimate Halloween weekend event — a tale of rivalry, romance, and one very unforgettable ride through Sleepy Hollow. Performance at 7:00 pm on October 30, 2026 and 3:00 pm on October 31-November 1, 2026, at UMD’s Marshall Performing Arts Center.

events.title: Holiday High Tea
events.description: ✨ Event Highlights: • Classic English Tea Service: Assorted sandwiches, sweets, scones and tea • Cash Bar: Specialty holiday-themed cocktails • Live Entertainment: A narrated synopsis of The Nutcracker by Minnesota Ballet dancers • Craft Corner: Decorate your own gingerbread cookie • Photo Station: Pose with ballerinas and Nutcracker characters in a turn-of-the-century-inspired setting • Discounted Minnesota Ballet merchandise & tickets available onsite 🎄 Special Offer for Families Receive $5 off children’s tickets when you purchase two or more using promo code TEA4THREE at checkout! 💎VIP Upgrades Available Treat yourself or someone special to the VIP experience, featuring: Priority seating at a private table A complimentary cocktail or mocktail A nutcracker-themed souvenir/toy Whether you’re continuing a family tradition or creating a new one, the Holiday High Tea with the Minnesota Ballet is a heartwarming way to celebrate the season.

events.title: The Nutcracker: A Duluth Tale
events.description: The holiday tradition that leaves every audience spellbound — this season featuring Tchaikovsky’s beloved score performed live by the Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra. Performance at 7:00 pm on December 11, and 3:00 pm on December 12-13, 2026, at DECC’s Symphony Hall. Tickets available through Ticketmaster, or save more than $20/ticket in fees by calling the Minnesota Ballet Box Office (218-733-7570) to reserve your seats.

events.title: Coppelia
events.description: One of the most beloved comic ballets of the 19th century, Coppélia tells the story of the clever and spirited Swanilda, who outwits an eccentric toymaker and wins back her wayward fiancé — all with irresistible charm and Léo Delibes’ glorious score. Pure joy from start to finish, and a perfect introduction to ballet for the whole family. Performance at 7:00 pm on March 12 and 3:00 pm on March 13-14, 2027, at UMD’s Marshall Performing Arts Center.

events.title: Family Discovery Day: International Archaeology Day
events.description: 🏺 Family Discovery Day: International Archaeology Day 📅 Saturday, October 17 ⏰ 11:00am–4:00pm 📍 Minnesota Discovery Center 💸 FREE Admission Join us for a free day of family fun as we celebrate International Archaeology Day at the Minnesota Discovery Center, featuring a FREE screening of Dora and the Lost City of Gold and hands-on archaeology activities for all ages! From 11:00am–2:00pm, enjoy archaeology activity stations in Taconite Square designed for explorers of all ages: 🥽 Experience the science of archaeology through VR technology 🪣 Sift for buried artifacts at a dig station 🍽️ Piece together broken plates like a real archaeologist 🪨 Learn about flintknapping 🏹 Try your hand at throwing an atlatl at a (cutout) bison Then, from 2:00-3:45pm, head to our theater for a FREE screening of Dora and the Lost City of Gold! Follow Dora and her friends on an adventure to save her parents and uncover the mystery of a lost Incan civilization. 🍿 Popcorn will be available for purchase for just $1 per bag. Whether you’re a budding archaeologist or simply looking for a fun family outing, there’s something for everyone to discover.

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free!

Complimentary water, juice, and light snacks are provided.

events.description: Peer into the past with convenient extended Research Center hours on October 29, 2026! During Late Night in the Research Center, the RC will be open from 10:00am to 8:00pm. Our super friendly, super knowledgeable staff will be ready and eager to help you trace your family genealogy, investigate regional history, find a good book to read, and more. 🔎📚 Late Night happens once a month, usually on the last Thursday (unless holidays interfere). Visiting the RC is always FREE!

events.title: The Research Center Presents: Ryan Vine’s The Cave: Poetry Reading & Book Signing
events.description: The Research Center Presents: Ryan Vine’s The Cave: Poetry Reading & Book Signing 🗓️ Date: Thursday, October 29 ⏰ Time: 5:00-7:30pm 📍 Place: MDC’s Theater 💸 Cost: FREE On Thursday, October 29 from 5:00-7:30pm, come listen to one of Minnesota’s most celebrated modern poets—Ryan Vine! Ryan will be reading from his latest poetry collection, The Cave, which explores the topics of fatherhood, generational trauma, and the ways place and lineage connect. It has been named one of the “Best Poetry Books of 2025” by the California Review of Books and “Top 5 of 2025” by Zenith Bookstore in Duluth, MN. Ryan was born and raised on the backwaters of the St. Louis River in the Fond Du Lac neighborhood of western Duluth. Along with being a poet, he is also a professor of English at the College of St. Scholastica. His honors include the Northeastern Minnesota Book Award, the Weldon Kees Award, the Robert Watson Poetry Prize, and more. Here’s the evening’s schedule: 🥂 5:00pm: Mingling and (free!)

events.title: Intrigue Chocolate Tasting Class
events.description: Intrigue Chocolate Tasting Class 📅 Date: November 12 ⏰ Time: 5:00-7:30pm 💵 Price: $48 (+ $2 processing fee) 🎟️ Register online: ! Indulge your sweet tooth with a 1-hour tasting and education session with local chocolate makers! During this class, you’ll delve into the science of flavor, gain insight into the chocolate-making process, and taste your way through various chocolate products (cacao tea, roasted cacao beans, and six different chocolate bars) with Aaron Barthel and Karl Mueller, co-owners of Intrigue Chocolate in downtown Chisholm, MN. 🍫☕🤤 About Aaron: Raised in Minnesota, Aaron has worn many hats throughout his life—he’s been a farmer, a botanist, a brewer, a baker, a chef, and a chocolate maker. He’s passionate about small-batch craft chocolate, and he loves experimenting with fruits, herbs, and spices. About Karl: Karl has an entrepreneurial spirit dedicated to taking on what he describes as the ultimate career challenge—building a sustainable and ethical business in the notoriously difficult industry of craft chocolate. He’s also interested in history, culture, and generally making the world a better place.

events.title: Call For Indigenous Artists
events.description: Call for Artists: Our Helpers, a Woodland Anishinaabe/Dakota Art Exhibition 🗓️ Apply now through Friday, November 13, 2026, 11:59pm 👥 Open to all Dakota, Ojibwe, and Ho-Chunk tribal citizens and descendants 👀 Accepting any visual art medium that can be physically displayed ❓ Questions? Accommodation needs? Email art.moira@gmail.com 🖋️ Application: View, fill out, and submit here Calling all Dakota, Ojibwe, and Ho-Chunk artists! MDC is excited to host Our Helpers, a Woodland Anishinaabe/Dakota Art Exhibition in partnership with local Indigenous artists Moira Villiard, Alexis Martinez, and Avery Makes Room For Them. Themed Our Helpers, the exhibit is an invitation to remember that we are never separate from the world around us. It honors the relationship between Indigenous peoples and the living world: animals, plants, water, sky, stars, and spirit. Artists and viewers alike are asked to consider not only who helps us humans, but also how we humans can become better helpers within the ecosystem of this evolving world in which we are all related and interconnected. Interested? Apply online! Applications are open now and close on November 13 at 11:59pm.

events.title: Family Discovery Day: Maamawai Giwii-Kikendamin (Together We Learn)
events.description: 📅 Saturday, November 14 ⏰ 10am–4pm 💸 FREE FOR ALL Join us and our friends from Bois Forte Heritage Center & Cultural Museum for Family Discovery Day: Maamawai Giwii-Kikendamin (Together We Learn) as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month through art, culture, food, music, and community. This FREE, family-friendly event is an opportunity to learn together through stories, shared experiences, and cultural traditions while supporting Indigenous artists, educators, and community members. Throughout the day, guests can participate in hands-on printmaking, enjoy an Ojibwe-inspired meal, and experience a vibrant cultural showcase featuring drumming, singing, and dancing. 🥁🎶 Join Fire in the Village, a collective of artists and cultural organizers, for a printmaking pop-up! Participants are invited to make and take a fabric patch featuring images of Aandeg (Crow), the Fire in the Village emblem, and other artwork created by Anishinaabe artist and director Annie Humphrey (Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe).

Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free!
