events.title: Pitch Your Friend
events.description: Think your friend’s a catch? This is your chance to make your case. Pitch your friend in a 5-minute presentation to a live crowd. Tell us who they are, why someone should date them, and make your best case. Then let the crowd decide who gave the best pitch. The winner gets a prize, and your friend might leave with a date (or a pretty good story). Whether you’re up there pitching your friend, looking to meet someone, or just here for the entertainment, come see what happens. Want to pitch your friend? Sign up here.

events.title: Bingo!
events.description: Might be time to start trusting your gut, your lucky numbers, or whatever superstition you swear works. Every Wednesday is bingo night, and it’s free to play. Good prizes, easy to win, and a solid midweek excuse to get out of the house.

events.title: Trivia
events.description: Clock in. Your brain shift starts now. Trivia is every Thursday night. There are eight rounds, including general knowledge, music, photos, and a few that make you question how you ever knew anything in the first place. Teams can be up to six people. There are prizes for the winners!

events.title: Halloween Family Jam
events.description: Know a kid who’s been sleeping in their costume and asking if they can wear it to the grocery store? This one’s for you. Family Jam is a family-friendly song and dance party with an interactive set from Dan the Monkeyman. Costumes encouraged, plus N/A drinks, ice cream, snacks, and maybe even some candy. It’s free, no registration required, and it’s all happening before the taproom opens. Stick around after for a slice from Wrecktangle Pizza.

events.title: Halloween Cookie Class
events.description: Are you ready to learn the art of sugar cookie decorating? Join us for a hands-on class where you’ll learn the basics and create a beautiful, 6-piece Halloween-themed cookie platter to take home. No experience necessary! What’s Included: Step-by-step guidance with a live demo displayed on an 84′′ screen Basic piping and filling techniques Cookies, icing, and sprinkles A tray to take your creations home Sugar cookie and royal icing recipes Access to a private Facebook community Perfect for a girls’ night out, date night, parent/child outing, or team-building event! Spaces are limited, so reserve your seat today!

events.title: Halloween Plant Swap
events.description: Join us for a Halloween Plant Swap! Bring your plants, cuttings, and plant-related goodies to buy, sell, swap, or browse. Halloween music will be playing, and costumes are encouraged! No plants to trade? No problem. Everyone is welcome to shop and hang out. Bringing plants to sell or swap? Please make sure they’re: Healthy and pest-free Rooted, or if unrooted, have visible nodes Labeled with the plant name to the best of your ability Priced, or have a price in mind if you’d rather sell than trade See ya, plant ghouls!

events.title: Horror Movie Trivia
events.description: Bring your trivia team for some seriously deep horror movie cuts. We’re talking slashers, supernatural scares, creepy classics, modern nightmares, and everything in between. So if you know your final girls, remember the names of the killers, and somehow know way too much about horror movies, this is your night. Teams of up to 6, free to play, prizes for the winners. Whether you can name every Friday the 13th sequel or just spend your weekends yelling at characters not to go into the basement, you’ll fit right in.

events.title: Wild Santa 5k & Reindeer Run
events.description: Wild Santa 5K on Saturday, December 12, is a fun run winding through the Lincoln Park Craft District of Duluth, MN. Registration includes a 5-piece Santa suit and a free cider, plus the whole crew can stick around for the all-ages after-party at Wild State Cider. Kids 8 and under can join the Reindeer Run! Reindeer Run registration includes a pair of antlers and entry into the Reindeer Run, a 1/4-mile fun run. Here’s what you can expect: Hundreds of Santas running around the neighborhood A sample of Bent Paddle Brewing Co.’s Christmas Cookie Ale Free cider before or after the race An all-ages after-party & more to be announced! This event is open to all ages. Find more details at wildsantarun.com.

events.title: Baptism River Barbecue Co.
events.description: Get ready for some seriously good Northwoods barbecue! Baptism River Barbecue Co. is rolling up to the Castle Danger Brewery taproom throughout 2026, serving their signature smoked meats and scratch-made sides crafted with locally sourced produce, responsibly raised animals, and hardwoods grown along Lake Superior’s North Shore. Founded by husband-and-wife team Dan and Kaylee Cahill Mathews, Baptism River Barbecue Co. brings a warm, community-focused vibe and unforgettable flavors to every visit. Whether you’re craving melt-in-your-mouth brisket, perfectly smoked pulled pork, or hearty homemade sides, their menu delivers comfort, craft, and true North Shore character. Come hungry, grab a pint, and enjoy some of the best barbecue around—right here on the harbor.. Follow them: Website: baptismriverbbq.com Instagram: @baptismriver_barbecueco Facebook: Baptism River Barbecue Co.

events.title: Fresh Hop Fest
events.description: Fresh Hop Fest is back at the Castle Danger Brewery Taproom on Saturday, October 17 from 11:00 AM–6:00 PM! Celebrate hop harvest season with us at the taproom! Fresh Hop Fest is a full day of fresh beer, live music, food, and fall fun. We’ll be pouring taproom-only fresh hop beer releases, brewed with freshly harvested hops to capture bright, vibrant hop flavors at their peak. Fresh Hop Beer Fresh Hop Pale Ale with Strata Hops Fresh Hop Mosaic IPA Fresh Hop Hazy IPA with Krush Hops Live Music All Day 11:00 AM–1:00 PM | Northeast Timberland Band 1:30–3:30 PM | Shorething 4:00–6:00 PM | Squid City Slingers Food Baptism River Barbecue will be serving up the goods throughout the event. Fall Fun Gourd Painting Celebrate fall by getting creative with guided gourd painting led by artist Eric Klepinger. Make your own harvest-season creation while enjoying the festivities. Mobile Zoo | 1:00–4:00 PM Cook’s Country Connection is bringing the farm to Fresh Hop Fest! Stop by between 1:00 and 4:00 PM for a unique mobile zoo experience featuring friendly animals including a llama, alpaca, mini horse, mini donkey, and goats.

events.description: The Northeast Timberland Band has been making music across the Duluth area for more than a decade, blending bluegrass, country rock, easy-listening classics, and modern acoustic favorites into an engaging live performance. events.description: Based out of Two Harbors, this North Shore quartet combines bass, guitar and some of the best vocal harmonies in the region.

events.title: Live Music: Squid City Slingers
events.description: Squid City Slingers are a high-energy Minnesota trio blending bluegrass, folk, country, and gypsy jazz into a sound that’s equal parts foot-stomping and heartfelt. Featuring driving stand-up bass, fiery fiddle, and flat-picking guitar, the band has built a growing following across the Twin Cities and Twin Ports through a mix of rich harmonies, original songs, and carefully selected covers. The group has performed at venues and festivals across the Midwest including Bent Paddle, Earth Rider, Gunflint Tavern, Bluegrass on the Black Festival, SquidFest, and the Minnesota Musician Showcase at Mall of America. With appearances on regional radio, television, podcasts, and an expanding festival schedule, Squid City Slingers continue to establish themselves as one of the Midwest’s rising acoustic acts. Their EP, Harbors & Highways, showcases the band’s Northwoods-inspired songwriting and energetic live sound.

events.title: Burger Joint
events.description: With a menu that consists of mouthwatering Burgers to satisfy your craving, Burger Joint not only has the tastiest combinations on the menu, but all ingredients are fresh and locally sourced. All patties are a premium blend of chuck, brisket and short rib.

events.title: Meat Raffle
events.description: Meat Raffle at Castle Danger Brewery Get ready for a true Minnesota classic. Join us in the taproom for an evening of cold beer, friendly competition, and community fun at our Meat Raffle, hosted by Two Harbors Moose Lodge 1463, featuring premium cuts from Zup’s Meat Market. Grab your tickets, gather your crew, and take your shot at winning some top-notch meats from Zup’s —all while supporting a great cause. All proceeds benefit the Moose Lodge and the local organizations they serve right here in the Two Harbors community.

events.title: Na-cho-Bizness
events.description: Na-cho Bizness is a vibrant Tex-Mex food truck serving up fresh tacos, burritos, nachos, and more across the North Shore. Locally loved for bold flavors, fun vibes, and great company — we bring the party wherever we park!

events.title: Books and Brews
events.description: Join the Two Harbors Public Library & Castle Danger Brewery every 3rd Tuesday of the month for Books & Brews! From 6-8pm, bring the book you are currently reading and chat with fellow book lovers. No specific genre, no specific title. Anything you are reading! Every book lover who brings their book to chat about will receive $1 off your first beer!

events.description: Taproom Loyalty members will receive double-points for their purchases on Wednesdays. Beers, a t-shirt from the merch store, another beer, a growler of your favorite beer to go, all double-points on Wednesdays. Not a Taproom Loyalty member? Join on your next trip to the brewery or sign up here.

events.title: Special Hours Taproom Opening at 4:00pm
events.description: The taproom will open late at 4:00 PM on Wednesday, October 21st. We will resume regular hours on Thursday, October 22nd, opening at 12:00 PM.

events.title: The Rainy Rose Food Trailer
events.description: Named after their daughters’ middle names, The Rainy Rose is a family-run food trailer owned by Mike and Amy Wahlman. This local favorite brings bold, Mexican-inspired comfort food to the North Shore — crafted with heart, heritage, and serious flavor. From crispy chimichangas and birria tacos to loaded nachos and their fan-favorite Cuban sandwich, the menu at The Rainy Rose offers something for everyone, including delicious jackfruit options for plant-based eaters. Every dish is made from scratch and rooted in Mike’s 20+ years of culinary experience and passion. So what are you waiting for? Grab a bite today!

events.title: Castle Danger Game Night
events.description: Castle Danger Game Nights Every Wednesday | 5:00 – 8:30pm Looking for a fun and welcoming way to spend your Wednesday evenings? Join us at Castle Danger Brewery for Game Nights. Game Nights bring people together to laugh, relax, and share good company over a table of cards, boards, or dice. Our taproom game collection will be open for everyone to use, ranging from classics to modern favorites. Guests are also encouraged to bring their own games to share with the group. Whether you’re coming with friends or flying solo, there’s always a place at the table. Game Nights are all about connection, laughter, and a relaxed community vibe, paired with your favorite Castle Danger beer. Come as you are, stay as long as you’d like, and let’s play!

events.title: Brother Ali with DJ Abilities
events.description: Brother Ali is a respected Hip Hop artist, speaker, and community leader. His two-decade resume includes ten critically-acclaimed albums, mentorships with iconic Hip Hop legends Chuck D and Rakim, and performances on late night shows with Jimmy Fallon and Conan O’Brien.His provocative and uplifting brand of Hip Hop has earned him coveted press features like Rolling Stone’s 40th anniversary edition and Source Magazine’s “Hip Hop Quotables”, while his outspoken social justice message has landed him on government watch lists. He’s also lectured at universities from Princeton to Stanford and delivered the keynote address at the Nobel Peace Prize Forum.When he’s not rocking the mic at Coachella or being arrested for civil disobedience in support of marginalized communities, Brother Ali travels the world learning and teaching Islamic Spirituality under some of today’s most renowned teachers. In addition to leading worship services and classes, he co-founded The Gemali Project, an organization that helps Muslim converts and spiritual seekers access the beauty of the Islamic tradition.

events.title: Friday Frequencies
events.description: When Ranger Danger is on the scene, only one thing is certain: you're going to have a good time. Their musical taste and fascination spans borders, genres and eras: From Afro-house to drum & bass, techno to yoga dub. Ranger Danger will cook up whatever the house is hungry for, and then they'll cook up some more.Ranger Danger isn’t just a performer, they’re a culture curator who believes dancing is a liberating practice. They embrace the wisdom of Emma Goldman, who said: “A revolution without dancing is a revolution not worth having.” Close your eyes, feel your body, free your mind and DANCE. Only YOU can set the floor on fire!

events.title: October Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: October Full Moon Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. October's full moon is the Hunter's Moon. Other autumnal names include Falling Leaves Moon, Drying Rice Moon, and Freezing Moon.

events.title: Best Stargazing November
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: New moon nights – night when the moon is absent from the sky – make for great stargazing. Here’s a great way to start – look due north after the sun has set and find the Big Dipper constellation [see photo] with its telltale 3-star handle and 4-star dipper. In the autumn, the dipper is at ‘6-o’clock’ with the dipper facing up/handle to the left.

events.title: Taurids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Taurids meteor shower is an annual meteor shower that occurs every November and is composed of two streams, the Southern Taurids and the Northern Taurids. The Taurids are known for producing bright fireballs, and 2025 is predicted to be a year with an increased number of them At peak viewing times during the Taurid meteor shower, you may be able to see about a half-dozen shooting stars per hour. The Northern Taurids are active between Oct 20 - Dec 10 and peak on Nov. 9-12.

events.title: Leonids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Leonids meteor shower offers clear-sky meteor rates of about 10 to 15 shooting stars per hour. They are active between Nov. 6 - 30 and will peak on Nov. 17-18. The Leonids are bright meteors and have a high percentage of persistent trains according to AMS. The Leonids' radiant is located in the sickle-shaped head of the constellation Leo, the lion. Leonid meteor hunting can be incredible, or a total bust. It all depends on where its parent body, Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, will be in its orbit and the kind of debris clumps that will be around when our planet passes through this comet's orbit.

events.title: November Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 1st of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. While the Frost Moon and Freezing Moon are self-explanatory, November's full moon is most known as the Beaver Moon. Beavers are quite active preparing for winter. Also known as the Mourning Moon, due to the increase in darkness.

events.title: Best Stargazing December
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: New moon nights – night when the moon is absent from the sky – make for great stargazing. Here’s a great way to start – look due north after the sun has set and find the Big Dipper constellation [see photo] with its telltale 3-star handle and 4-star dipper. In the winter, the dipper is at ‘3-o’clock’ with the handle hanging down.

events.title: Geminids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Geminids meteor shower occurs between November 19 to December 24 and this year will peak on the nights of December 13 and 14. The shower can produce 130 to 140 bright, white, fast meteors per hour on a clear sky. The debris that falls onto Earth's atmosphere during this meteor shower comes from the asteroid Phaethon. The meteor shower's radiant is located in the constellation Gemini, which rises around sunset.

events.title: December Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 2nd of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. December's full moon is known as the Cold Moon or Long Nights Moon. In addition to the shortest daylight day of the year, the Long Nights Moon pertains to the amount of time the moon is above the horizon. It takes a high trajectory across the sky because it is opposite to the low sun.

events.title: January Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 3rd of 3 supermoons A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. The January full moon is most often known as the Wolf Moon because it is the month hungry wolves howl in the night. It is also known as the Stay Home, or Quiet, Moon as cold temps set in and we want to snuggle in and stay home.

events.title: Introduction to 3D Modeling and Printing: From Idea to Object, with Tim Lutgen
events.address: 5503 W. Range View Drive, Hurley, WI
events.description: Have you ever looked at a broken piece of plastic, had a missing part for a project, or had a creative idea in your head and wished you could simply print the solution? “Introduction to 3D Modeling and Printing: From Idea to Object” with Tim Lutgen is the perfect place to turn those digital concepts into physical reality! Slated for three afternoons in a row, from 4 to 6 p.m. on Oct. 19-21, at Hurley High School, this course is designed for adults who are curious about the “how-to” behind 3D printing. Tim will demystify the process by breaking it down into two core components: designing, using CAD (Computer-Aided Design) software, and printing, learning how to “slice” your model and operate a 3D printer to bring it to life. No prior engineering experience is needed, just a willingness to experiment and a bit of patience as we master these tools together. Just $45, including the cost of materials!

events.title: Remembering Alex – Piano Dedication
events.description: Join us as we dedicate our new Kawai KG-3E conservatory piano in the theatre mezzanine and celebrate the memory of Alex Marciniak, from whose estate we acquired the baby grand.Alex Marciniak made a lasting impact on the Gogebic Range. His career spanned over 30 years as an instructor at Gogebic Community College, where he taught music appreciation, speech, art history, film history and piano. “Extracurricular” activities ran the gamut from pianist, actor, director, and entertainer. His exuberant personality and generous spirit inspired many.Here at the Theatre, Alex was instrumental in founding the Gogebic Range Players, an ensemble of theatre enthusiasts. He directed many theatre productions, from intimate dinner theater plays, including “Driving Miss Daisy,” to large stage musicals, most notably “Showboat, “ “Grease,” “Forever Plaid,” “The Taffetas,” and “Chicago.”

events.title: The Monster
events.description: Spooktacular Silent Cinema: The Monster (1925) Date: Saturday, October 24th Time: 7:00 PM Tickets: $20 Step back into the golden age of horror-comedy with a special screening of the 1925 silent classic, The Monster! Directed by Roland West and starring horror legend Lon Chaney, this spine-tingling flick follows meek clerk and aspiring sleuth Johnny Goodlittle. Eager to solve a rash of mysterious highway abductions and win the heart of the lovely Betty, Johnny tracks sinister clues to a spooky, isolated asylum. There, he and his companions fall into the trap of the unhinged Dr. Ziska (Chaney), who has far more in store for them than a simple tour. Lock the doors and prepare for bizarre experiments, strange servants, and plenty of classic chilling thrills. Featuring Live Musical Accompaniment Enhance your experience with a live performance on our historic Barton Organ, performed by in-house composer and accompanist Tim Mesun. Tim will bring every jump-scare, shadow, and comedic twist to life in real-time, delivering an authentic 1920s moviegoing experience you won’t want to miss. Get your tickets today for an unforgettable night of classic horror, humor, and live music!

events.title: Harmony on Silver Memory Choir
events.description: Harmony on Silver is a choir consisting of people living with memory changes, such as dementia or Alzheimer’s, their care-partners, friends, and community members. We are dedicated to enriching lives through intergenerational choral music, and our mission is to create opportunities for people to connect and thrive through singing together. We are excited to express our love of the Hurley/Ironwood and surrounding areas through service, artistry, and inclusion with a particular focus on the inclusion of people living with memory and thinking changes. events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: Our Town
events.description: Theatre North Presents: Our Town, by Thornton Wilder, Directed by: Helen Fashbaugh Show Dates and Times: February 18, 19, 20, 26 and 27 at 7:00pm Matinees February 21 and 28 at 2:00pm Thornton Wilder’s American classic, Pultizer-prize winning Our Town, explores the universal human experience of life, love, and death. Set in the fictional small town of Grover’s Corners, New Hampshire, the story follows the everyday lives of the Gibbs and Webb families across three acts. The play is famous for its minimalist approach, often performed on a bare stage with no curtains or scenery, relying on pantomime and a narrator called the Stage Manager to guide the audience into its intimacy and truth. The narrative is divided into three distinct acts: Act I: Daily Life: Introduces the town’s routine, highlighting the simple chores, gossip, and rhythms of small-town life. Act II: Love and Marriage: Follows the childhood friends, George Gibbs and Emily Webb, as they fall in love, grow up, and get married. Act III: Death and Eternity: Concludes years later with Emily’s tragic death in childbirth.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: Meet and Greet with Alex Messenger, "The Ice on the Lake"
events.description: Meet and Greet with Alex Messenger, "The Ice on the Lake" Friday, October 16 from 11 am - 1 pm Drury Lane Books, Grand Marais Come down anytime during the two hour event to have your books signed! We will have both of Messengers' books on hand, his first, The Twenty-Ninth Day, and also his recent novel, The Ice on the Lake. Event is free and open to the public. While the shop is mobility aid accessible, our Meet and Greets happen during regular store hours which could make getting around our small space difficult. Please feel welcome to chat with the bookseller on duty for any assistance needed. The Ice on the Lake is a novel of resilience and determination-both to survive the fury of nature and to reconcile with the ghosts of the past. The harsh winters of Duluth, Minnesota, don’t bother Hugh McLaren. Decades after the death of his wife and estrangement from his children, the only respite from his troubled thoughts comes from ice fishing alone on the windswept expanse of Lake Superior. Out on the ice, Hugh can drop a line in search of monsters of the deep and be free of his own demons.

events.title: Possibilities Quartet
events.description: Possibilities Quartet Friday, October 16th, 6:00 pm - 7:30 pm Grand Marais Public Library This 90-minute performance includes pieces composed and arranged by local jazz musician Greg Moore, as well as operatic and Latin pieces. The program is designed to be engaging and welcoming to the general public, with an emphasis on performance rather than formal instruction. Audience questions will be welcomed throughout the evening. Appropriate for all ages, community members are invited to arrive at 5:30 PM for access to the best seats. Formed in early 2024, the Possibilities Quartet is a regional chamber ensemble committed to bringing high-quality live music to both public audiences and schools across northern Minnesota and northwestern Wisconsin. In addition to public performances, the quartet is actively engaged in music education outreach, working with middle and high school programs through performances, masterclasses, and sectional instruction. Members of the group perform with several prominent regional groups including Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra, Borealis, Arrowhead Chorale, Lake Superior Chamber Orchestra, and LOON opera.

events.title: Buffalo Galaxy LIVE at Up Yonder
events.description: Buffalo Galaxy LIVE at Up Yonder Friday and Saturday, October 16th and 17th from 8:00 - 11:00 pm Up Yonder on 61, Grand Marais Buffalo Galaxy will be playing not one but TWO NIGHTS at Up Yonder! Deep Space, Light Speed, Bluegrass! Buffalo Galaxy (Minneapolis, MN) is where heavy hitting psychedelia meets old timin’ bluegrass. Their songwriting, patience, and personalities prove they go deep! Banjo, Mandolin, Upright Bass, and Acoustic Guitar play off each other reaching both interstellar space and a universal familiarity. Their song catalog ranges from short and sweet Bill Monroe to here and now Lil Nas X. As well as catchy originals like "Time Machine" and long renditions of Grateful Dead classics. Up Yonder on 61 is located in "Uptown" Grand Marais and serves elevated bar food 'til 10 p.m.

events.title: David Hahn Art Days
events.description: David Hahn Art Days Thursday, October 15 & Friday, October 16, 2026 10:00 am - 2:00 pm Grand Marais Art Colony Studio 21 David Hahn was a beloved community-member, artist who passed away in 2022. He attended Washington University School of Fine Arts and the University of Minnesota. David was Art Director for Miller Publishing. After retiring to Hovland, David focused on watercolor and enjoyed teaching youth classes at the Art Colony as well as working within the public school, creating portrait cards for the Viking athletic teams. His generous memorial gifts support the funding for this event. Free art stations will be set up for participants to explore various art activities. Youth 8 and younger must be accompanied by an adult Recurring daily.

events.title: Family Weekend
events.description: Family Weekend Friday, Oct 16 - Saturday, Oct 17, 2026 North House Folk School, Grand Marais Here in Minnesota, kids get a long weekend in October known to most as “MEA.” Use that school break for a family folk school break and come on up to Grand Marais for Family Weekend at North House Folk School! Fall weather, contra dancing, and families learning crafts of all kinds on the shore of Lake Superior—what could be better?! During Family Weekend, which coincides with Grand Marais' annual Moose Madness Family Festival , over a dozen classes are on offer, some for kids only, others for adults and kids to take together. From cooking to fiber arts, woodworking to blacksmithing, there is a skill to learn for everyone. The weekend includes both formal classes that require registration ahead of time as well as drop-in activities and evening programs that are free and require no pre-registration.

events.title: Moose Madness Family Festival
events.description: Moose Madness: Big Fun in the North Woods! Celebrate Minnesota’s favorite long weekend in the heart of Cook County during Moose Madness 2026 (October 15–17)! This beloved annual festival transforms Grand Marais into a giant, moose-themed playground filled with family-friendly adventures, local shopping, and outdoor fun. Whether you’re racing alongside our official mascot, Murray the Moose, or soaking in the crisp autumn air along the shores of Lake Superior, there is something around every corner for explorers of all ages. This year’s lineup blends cherished traditions with exciting new ways to explore town at your own pace: Murray’s Grand Marais Trivia Trail (New!): Embark on a self-guided Bandwango digital quest across town, answering fun moose trivia at local stops to earn an exclusive "Moose Expert" 2026 collectible sticker. The Moose Correspondent & Northern Moose Alliance (New!): Catch real-time event updates, live dispatches, and fascinating wildlife insights from our roving field reporter throughout the weekend. Be sure to learn more about Adam and his work with Northern Moose Alliance . Double Medallion Hunt: Double the search!

events.title: Rock Wrapping with Jill Terrill
events.description: Wrapped Rocks w/Jill Terrill (How does she do it? Want to find out?) Joy & Co., Grand Marais Third Fridays, 1 - 3 pm Aug 21st Sept 18th Oct 16th If you have been to Joy & Company lately, you have probably noticed a growing collection of stunning wrapped rocks. Learn the art of turning ordinary stones into beautiful, wearable, or display-ready pieces using leather‐wrapping techniques. This class covers: Material basics — choosing the right rocks, wrap , and tools ( please bring a rock if you have one you especially love, otherwise rocks will be provided) Core wrapping techniques Design planning — how to choose a wrap style that fits each stone Finishing methods — polishing, securing ends, or display stands Students leave with one or 2 finished wrapped rocks and the skills to continue at home. All materials included. $20 Limited seating. Reservations will be taken, please call the store 218-387-1004 and let the person answering the phone how many and what date. Depending on will run additional classes with possible open dates. If you have a larger group or different date in mind, please don't hesitate to ask. Recurring monthly on the 3rd Friday.

events.description: Joe Diethelm LIVE at Cascade! Joes musical performances are lively and interactive, encouraging singing, dancing, and other participatory activities. events.title: Northern Lotus Meditation
events.description: Meditation can be a path to self-awareness and compassion toward others, but it can also be a path to better overall health and well-being, mentally, emotionally, and physically. Experience a mindful group meditation practice in a warm and inclusive environment. Whether you're a seasoned meditator or a complete beginner, all are welcome. No prior experience is needed; just an open heart and a willingness to explore this path. With Rev. Zahir Orest EVERY WEDNESDAY 7:00 - 8:00 pm If you're new, arrive at 6:45 for meditation instructions. 7:00 – 7:20 Sitting meditation 7:20 – 7:30 Walking breath practice (Kinhin) 7:30 – 7:50 Sitting meditation 7:50 – 8:00 Formal Exit You are welcome to join in either or both of the sitting meditations. Floor cushions and chairs are provided. Free-will donations are much appreciated. Contact Rev. Zahir Roman Orest at (612) 865-4369 for more information or with any questions. Recurring weekly on Wednesday.

events.title: The Root Beer Lady | Dorothy Molter Play
events.description: The Root Beer Lady | Dorothy Molter Play Thursday, October 22, 7:00 p.m. Arrowhead Center for the Arts, Grand Marais Friends of the Boundary waters presents a touring production of The Root Beer Lady . Written and presented by Kim Schultz, The Root Beer Lady tells the story of the indomitable Dorothy Molter, the last legal non-indigenous resident of the Boundary Waters. The story reflects the beauty and hardships of Molter’s solitary yet satisfying life beginning in 1934. The play, funny and passionate, explores her independence, fortitude, and love of nature. Molter pushes back against the premise that her time in the North Woods made her the “Loneliest Woman in America,” as the Saturday Evening Post claimed in 1952. Kim Schultz is a nationally and internationally acclaimed writer, actor, and solo show artist working across mediums. This marks Kim’s third solo show. The tour is produced by Bourgoin Productions.

events.title: Date Night in the Barrel Room
events.description: Join us for a Date Night in the Barrel Room at North Shore Winery! We are open late on Thursdays, so grab your date and come down to the winery for music from 6:00 to 8:00 pm featuring fingerstyle guitar master and highly regarded bluesman Gordon Thorne. Gordon Thorne picked up a guitar 30 years ago and hasn’t put it down since. He spent years mining early American blues and jazz, blending them with his own style, and serves up what he calls, “the modern sounds of yesterday – today.” Known as the meanest fingerpicker in Northern Minnesota it is where he spends his time working, raising kids and playing a little guitar. Recurring weekly on Thursday.

events.description: The Wisconsin Canoe Heritage Museum invites you to join them for thier annual end-of-the-season celebration. events.title: Glow Hike
events.description: Registration is not required for this event. However, if you want to ensure you get a glow in the dark goodie bag, registration and payment are strongly encouraged online. Each registered participant will receive a glow in the dark goodie bag with stick, bracelet and necklace. Goodie bags will be available for walk-in registrants until gone. Discover things that glow with black light flashlights.

events.title: Paint & Sip: Pumpkin with Dried Flowers
events.description: Update (9/23/26): Only 9 spots left! Sign up for a Paint & Sip at 172 Bites & Brews in Trego, WI on Saturday, Oct. 17 at 5:00pm! We are creating the Pumpkin with Dried Flowers for $45 per person! The 15" Wood Pumpkin will be painted in whatever colors you choose, then we will put on the dried flowers and pour resin over them as the glue. This is a fun, easy project!! Class max is 14 people and approx 2 hours. I will walk you through the whole project and help along the way. No experience necessary. Sign up by calling: 715-349-5169, email: jellybeanascp@gmail.com, Facebook Messenger or jellybeanascraftpaint.com/classes . You can pay at the class (cash or card) or using the Ticket Link. The $45 covers the class fee & materials. Food & Drinks to be paid to 172 Bites & Brews. If you want one of their charcuterie boards, call them ahead of the class.

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: Lord of the Rings Movie Trilogy Trivia
events.description: One does not simply walk into LOTR trivia. There is a team registration form that never sleeps. Here's a link: https://duluthcider.com/events/lord-of-the-rings-trivia The Fellowship of the Ring came out 25 years ago [pause for gasp of realization that we’re getting old]. Those films have held up better than anything else since, so we’re celebrating with a special Lord of the Rings Movie Trilogy Trivia Night! Yes, the extended editions are fair game. We will not be diving into any other Tolkien films, just the original trilogy. Teams of 1-8 players (must be age 21+) for this free event. Pre-register at the link below to ensure a spot, or show up and hope for the best. The top 3 teams will win prizes for their quarter century of dedication to this incredible franchise, plus a special prize for the team with the best name. Show up a little early to get the best seats in the house, as the night is likely to fill up. Email info@duluthcider.com with any questions, and we’ll see you at Trivia on Thursday October 22 at 7pm!

events.title: Lakeside Yoga Stretch
events.description: Admission $12.00 Location NLDC Lodge or Amphitheater Description Wherever you are in your yoga practice, this class is for you. Lakeside Yoga is a gently paced class that encourages deep release in the body's major muscle groups. Through mindful stretching, breathwork, and intentional movement, students can increase flexibility, ease chronic pain, and improve their overall range of motion. Lakeside Yoga also helps build strength and cultivates balance in both body and mind. Whether you're new to yoga or a seasoned practitioner, you'll leave feeling grounded, refreshed, and restored. All are welcome. Class will be held at the Discovery Center indoors. We suggest participants bring a yoga mat and water. Class will be held at the Discovery Center in the Main Lodge or the Ampitheater (weather dependent). All levels welcome. Charge for each class is $12.00 to be paid on the day of class. No registration required. Saturday 9:30 AM - 10:30 AM. Registration is not required for yoga and takes place weekly. We do not allow the ability to register online in advance, as payment is taken at the door. Please be prepared to pay $12.00 on the day of class.

events.title: Iron County Historical Museum
events.description: Plan an adventure at the Iron County Historical Society Museum. Built in 1893 as the town hall for the now-vanished Town of Vaughn, the museum building was sold the following April to serve as the courthouse of Iron County. The Museum offers you three full floors of display from history of iron mining to railroads, timber to veterans, home life to faith based articles. The museum is filled with many old photos showing life in the past. May thru October MON/WED/FRI/SAT 1OAM-2PM, NOVEMBER - APRIL WED/FRI/SAT.

events.title: Family Fun with Spooky Friends
events.description: Family Fun with Spooky Friends Saturday, October 17th 10:00am – 1:00pm Drop by the Visitor Center to learn about bats and wolves as we kick off Wolf Week (October 18-24) and Bat Week (October 24-31)! Enjoy family-friendly games and activities while learning about how important bats and wolves are to our ecosystem. · Meet Echo the bat! · Study tracks, skulls, and furs · Trace a life size wolf cut-out to bring home · Make a plaster cast of a wolf track · And much more!

events.title: Animal Spotlight Hour: Wolves
events.description: Drop in anytime during the hour to learn from a Discovery Center Naturalist as we explore the amazing creatures found in our own backyards! For this month's Animal Spotlight, we will explore the wild world of wolves. Come find out what makes these charismatic critters special! Drop in anytime during the hour, explore animal artifacts, learn fun animal facts, and ask a naturalist your wildlife questions. Registration is preferred, but not required. This event is offered free of charge to participants due to generous funds provided by St. Matthias Thrift Shop. Saturday, October 24th, 10:00 AM - 11:00 AM.

events.title: StoryWalk ® Trail Program: One Wolf Howls by Scotti Cohn
events.description: Join a Discovery Center Naturalist as we celebrate Wolf Awareness Week with this month's book One Wolf Howls by Scotti Cohn. This is a fun rhyming book that teaches kids about wolf behavior, the months of the year, and counting from one to twelve. It follows a pack's seasonal activities, such as howling, hunting, and caring for pups. The narrative takes readers on a year-long journey from January to December, matching seasonal environments with an ever-growing pack of wolves. Please register the child/children names only. Space is limited and registration is required by 10/23/26. These programs are free of charge and are sponsored by the Shepherd-Howells Fund. Everyone is welcome to participate. Proceeds from treat sales benefit Friends of Copper Falls State Park. The event is sponsored by Friends of Copper Falls State Park.

events.title: Canning 101 with Marsha Fairfield
events.description: Learn the ins and outs of canning food for preservation purposes! In this workshop participants will learn how to preserve food by using both water bath and pressure canning processes. Discussions will include which process to use and why, canning and food safety, and basic recipes to try at home. Marsha Fairfield has been canning for over twenty years. events.description: Admission $12.00 Location NLDC Lodge or Amphitheater Description Wherever you are in your yoga practice, this class is for you. events.title: Soldiers of the American Revolution - Buhl Public Library
events.description: The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present Soldiers of the American Revolution with Arn Kind of Historical Experiences. These free history events will travel to participating ALS libraries October 14-November 20, 2026. On this 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence join Arn Kind for an event all about the American Revolution. This in depth presentation puts audience members into the life of a revolutionary soldier with historical artifacts, uniforms, and hands-on experiences. Audiences will enjoy learning about the causes of the revolution and how it led to the birth of the United States of America. This two hour program is suited for ages 10 and up. These free programs are being offered at the following locations: Wednesday, October 14, 1:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. - Coleraine Public Library Thursday, October 15, 10:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. - Marble Public Library Thursday, October 15, 4:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. - Calumet Public Library Friday, October 16, 1:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. - Buhl Public Library Saturday, October 17, 10:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. - Eveleth Public Library Monday, October 19, 10:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. - Cook Public Library Tuesday, October 20, 10:00 a.m.

events.title: Cataloging Workday
events.description: Cataloging Workday Tuesday, November 24, 2026 – 10:00 to3:00 In Person at ALS Audience: Horizon and BLUEcloud Catalogers with questions Description: ALS catalogers assemble to offer expertise and advice during a day of work! This session will focus on special topics and questions staff have about any aspect of cataloging, brainstorming common issues, and some discussion of cataloging standards across the ALS system. We will be working on cataloging items, so bring up to 15 items and questions to go with them. We suggest bringing a few special items like kits or "library of things" items to discuss, and there will be access to OCLC records. There will be a half hour brown bag lunch/break at noon, and attendees can come and go as they please. Note: if possible, please bring any laptops or relevant tech to help you work. In order to address issues equitably, please only bring up to 15 examples you’d like us to work on.

events.title: The Northland Beckons: Writing in Haiku - Grand Rapids Area Library
events.description: The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present free writing workshops at participating ALS libraries from October 9-30, 2026. These workshops, presented by author Sandra Hisakuni, are titled: The Northland Beckons: Writing in Haiku . Grow your creativity and writing skills in this fun haiku workshop. Writers will learn the structure and form of haiku, its origins in Japanese literature, and how Sandra Hisakuni connects this writing practice to Minnesota's Northwoods. Workshop attendees will explore this powerful tool for mindfulness, joyful reflection, and playful expression. Writers will use words and art to create their own haiku masterpiece to take home. This program is 1 hour long and suited for adults, teens, and children ages 10 and up. events.description: Cheesehead, clean comedians Mack & Harmston's duet stand up show in support of a pro-union election. General public welcome & encouraged! Much needed levity before the midterms. $15 online at MaryMackComedy.com or cash at door. Free with current union ID. Info & tickets at MaryMackComedy.com.

events.venue: The Caddy Shack Indoor Golf & Pub
events.description: Join us for a hilarious night of live dating with comedians crashing the entire night making it hilarious and somehow worse Due to high demand, Funny Bachelors is coming back to Duluth for one night only 💥 📍 Wednesday Nov 11th at the caddy shack! Doors 6PM | 7PM showtime The most unhinged dating show is back, where real singles go on actual blind dates LIVE on stage, while a panel of comedians roasts, riffs, and lovingly sabotages the whole thing using every nuance of a first date as target practice. It’s part comedy show, part reality dating experiment, and fully chaotic fun. We have expanded to multiple cities and states, been on interviewed on multiple new sources, and been featured in the 10k laughs festival! 💘 Whether you’re hunting for love, drama, or just a night of laugh-out-loud mischief..Funny Bachelors is the wild ride you didn’t know you needed. For casting information, please email FunnyBachelorscasting@gmail.com We look for singles of all ages, genders, sexual orientations, someone comfortable being filmed.

events.description: The Squid City Slingers are a folkgrass band from Duluth, Minnesota, playing original songs and unexpected covers that somehow sound like they were always meant to be played this way. With fiddle, upright bass, mandolin, banjo, and guitar leading the way, the band puts its own spin on everything from folk and bluegrass standards to songs you never expected to hear played by 27 strings (until one inevitably breaks). Featured by NPR's Great American Folk Show and PBS Backroads, the Squid City Slingers have become known for performances that feel just as at home on a festival stage as they do at a neighborhood brewery or outdoor concert series. Their shows are filled with musicianship, personal stories, and the kind of easygoing energy that makes first-time listeners feel like they've been listening for years. Whether they're introducing an original or reinventing a familiar favorite, the goal is always the same: play great songs, have a great time, and give people something to tell their friends about.

events.description: 8:00 PM Show The Driftless Revelers formed in the second spring of the first global pandemic of the 21st century, with one ear turned toward the shellac platters and Victrola virtuosos of the early to mid 20th century, and the other ear glued to the soundscapes of the 1960's & 1970's American freak-folk scene. events.title: Jaerv
events.description: Jaerv + The OK Factor The award-winning Swedish quintet Jaerv, present an extroverted, vigorous and heartfelt folk music with influences from both jazz and pop music. Together, the five members have created a homogeneous, vivid sound which has established Jaerv on the folk music scene as well as in many other forums. Rooted in several different musical traditions, Jaerv offers a varied stage performance where vocal, five-voiced tunes blend in with energetic dances and free improvisations. Jaerv is an internationally well known act and has toured the U.S., Japan, Spain, Scotland, Ireland, Finland and Norway among other countries. They have received various rewards and recognitions from a vast number of cultural foundations such as the Royal Academy of Music, The Swedish Arts Council and The American-Swedish Foundation. Their discography includes three full length albums and a number of singles and collaborations, featuring eg. the Japanese Koto-master Hiroe Morikawa, the American duo The OK Factor, award-winning choir Vocal Art Ensemble and the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra.

events.title: Indecent Proposal
events.description: We’re kicking off the weekend back at one of our favorite spots — Cobalt Lounge at Black Bear Casino Resort — on Friday, October 16 from 9 PM to midnight. There’s always something special about this room for us. The staff, the crowd, the energy — every time we come back, it feels like a place that truly gets what Indecent Proposal is about. So we’re coming in ready to start the weekend the right way with a full night of live music, familiar favorites, and the kind of moments that make a Friday night feel bigger than it should. If you’ve seen us here before, you already know how this goes. If not, this is a damn good night to fix that. Come spend your Friday with us at Black Bear. Come out and get Indecent 😈😎🎸🤘💜 www.indyp218.com Indecent Proposal is a band out of Duluth, Minnesota, built around connection, feel, and songs that hold up in a room full of people. Blending modern alt-rock, groove-driven covers, and emotionally grounded originals, the band focuses on moments you can feel as much as hear. Their live shows move fluidly between intimacy and release—quiet verses, loud hearts, and choruses that come back at you from the crowd.

events.title: Ian Alexy: Every Third Saturday at Sir Ben's
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Ian Alexy plays solo acoustic (with looping and effects, of course) on the third Saturday of every month at Sir Benedict's in Duluth. Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life.

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz & Jimmy Rogers | Sir Bens Tavern
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.description: Wilson Fairchild is more than just a country music duo—they’re a force of nature in the industry, known for their unique blend of traditional and contemporary sounds. Comprising cousins Wil and Langdon Reid, Wilson Fairchild brings a rich heritage of music and storytelling to every song they create. With deep roots in the heart of the Shenandoah Valley, their music is a reflection of their upbringing, life experiences, and unwavering love for country music. Wilson Fairchild, the acclaimed duo of Wil and Langdon Reid, continues a musical legacy that spans three generations. Sons of Statler Brothers legends Don Reid and Harold Reid, the cousins proudly carry forward their fathers’ enduring influence on country and gospel music while carving out a sound distinctly their own. As Gaither recording artists, Wilson Fairchild has spent more than 15 years captivating audiences nationwide with their seamless harmonies, quick wit, and heartfelt songwriting. Their performances blend beloved classics with fresh originals, creating an evening filled with laughter, musical excellence, and cherished memories.

events.title: Dan and Faith
events.description: Playing a set at Wussow's Concert Cafe Dan and Faith are a touring New Hampshire-based husband and wife singer-songwriter duo who describe their music as dream-inspired folk. Daniel Senie (guitar, banjo, harmonica, vocals) and Faith Senie (mandolin, acoustic bass guitar, ukulele, mountain dulcimer, vocals) tap into the imagery captured in dreams, as well as everyday life, in crafting their original songs that tell the stories of people and places, real and imagined. Among the duo’s five studio albums are Who We Are (2024), Then and Now (2020), Seeking (2016), and Simple Grace (2014). An earlier album and a live EP are no longer available. Dan and Faith’s sound is rooted in tight, interwoven vocal harmonies, supported by varied instrumentation and an occasional a cappella treatment. In live performances and radio interviews, they introduce or follow most songs with additional storytelling about the characters and places in each one, and the inspiration behind them. The duo got their musical start in New England and now travel throughout the U.S.

events.title: Jeffrey Foucault
events.venue: Cedar Lounge - Earth Rider Brewery taproom
events.description: In two decades on the road Jeffrey Foucault has become one of the most distinctive voices in American music, refining a sound instantly recognizable for its simplicity and emotional power. With a string of critically acclaimed studio albums – “Stark, literate songs that are as wide open as the landscape of his native Midwest” (The New Yorker), "Beat-up troubadour folk whittled to dolorous perfection” (Uncut), “Songwriting Brilliance,” (Irish Times) – he’s built a brick-and-mortar international touring career and a devoted following that includes luminaries like Van Dyke Parks, Greil Marcus, Gregory Alan Isakov, and Don Henley. In September of 2024 Jeffrey Foucault released THE UNIVERSAL FIRE (Fluff & Gravy, 9/6/24), his first album of entirely new material since 2018. A series of high-voltage performances cut live in one room, the album is both a working wake – Foucault lost his best friend and drummer Billy Conway, to cancer in 2021 – and a meditation on the nature of beauty, artifact, and loss.

events.title: Teague Alexy: Monday Residency at Sir Ben's
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Teague Alexy performs every Monday at Sir Benedict's Tavern in Duluth, MN. Teague's new album EFFERVESCENT now streaming. Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs.

events.title: Hadestown
events.description: WELCOME TO HADESTOWN, WHERE A SONG CAN CHANGE YOUR FATE. HADESTOWN, the acclaimed Broadway musical phenomenon by singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and director Rachel Chavkin makes its long-awaited West End premiere in February 2024 at the Lyric Theatre. ‘An epic celebration of music, togetherness and hope’ (Forbes) HADESTOWN is the winner of 8 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the Grammy Award® for Best Musical Theatre Album. HADESTOWN takes you on an unforgettable journey to the underworld and back, intertwining two mythic love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone. A deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience, HADESTOWN invites you to imagine how the world could be.

events.title: Lumanyano Mzi: Hadestown National Tour | DECC Symphony Hall
events.description: Currently on the road performing with the Hadestown National Tour. Check out the upcoming dates and catch the show in a city near you! HADESTOWN: COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go.

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

events.title: Sugarland
events.description: Grammy Award-winning pair Jennifer Nettles and Kristian Bush are refreshing their musical visions while staying true to an authentic sound and emotive songwriting that has made Sugarland a ubiquitous with Country music duos. The Georgia natives released their first new music in seven years with “Still The Same” setting the tone for their joint venture with Big Machine Records and UMG Nashville. Since the band’s inception in 2002, Sugarland has sold nearly 10 million albums domestically, achieving high-mark sales with PLATINUM-certified THE INCREDIBLE MACHINE, 2X PLATINUM LOVE ON THE INSIDE and 3X PLATINUM TWICE THE SPEED OF LIFE as well as ENJOY THE RIDE. Their most popular songs include PLATINUM-certified “All I Want to Do” and “Stay,” 2X PLATINUM “Stuck Like Glue” as well as GOLD-certified “Baby Girl,” “It Happens,” “Settlin’,” “Something More” and “Want To.” Sugarland has also earned seven No. 1 singles to date and amassed over 260 million on-demand streams.

events.title: Sugarland
events.description: To hear Jennifer Nettles tell it, it’s a brand new day in Sugarland. Despite winning multiple Grammy, CMA and ACM awards—and selling more than 8 million records—the country-music duo of Nettles and Kristian Bush is embracing a creative rebirth, a musical awakening that permeates their adventurous fourth album, The Incredible Machine. “We are in a place of discovery,” Jennifer says. “It is the essence of who we are as people in this band. There is never a moment where we think, ‘This is good enough.’ There’s always a place for growth.” A growth that Kristian says has been encouraged by their fans, their record label, and, most importantly, by the genre-bending, all-are-welcome country-music industry. “It’s as if the industry and the culture have singled out the biggest risks we’ve taken on a record, a song like ‘Stay’ for example, and celebrated those,” he says gratefully. “They’ve embraced us at those times. We’ve tried to learn from that and this is what we’ve made.” And what they’ve created is a dynamic masterwork.

events.title: Payton Sullivan
events.description: Payton Sullivan is redefining what country music sounds like from the shores of Hawaii. Born in Florida and raised near Nashville, she rebuilt her life—and her sound—on an island ranch. Blending Nashville storytelling with island rhythm, she calls it The Ultimate Coastal Cowgirl. Her latest singles, produced by Kristian Bush, showcase her signature mix of grit, grace, and empowerment. “It’s country music with sand on its boots and salt on its lips,” Sullivan says. “It’s where I found my voice.” She will hit the road as direct support for Sugarland’s 2026 Ride or Die fall tour spanning across 24 U.S tour dates. Tour dates and new music can be found at paytonsullivan.com.

events.title: Ross Thorn
events.venue: Cedar Lounge - Earth Rider Brewery taproom
events.description: There’s a type of band that doesn’t just play songs — they collect them, test-drive them, stretch them, condense them, and send them back out however they’re meant to be. Fellow Travelers belong in that category. At the heart of it all is Max Niemann: armed with a six-string guitar, a harmonica rack, and a catalog of songs that feel lived-in – whether it’s a front porch blues or a sprawling piece of electric alchemy. With a pastoral upbringing in northern Wisconsin, Ross Thorn’s music emanates as a warm and soulful hymn, waking up optimistically beside a snow-covered window. His sharply crafted and often humorous lyrics—distinctly reminiscent of great folk artists like John Prine—reveal internal struggles of empathy, questions of human character and virtue, and a search for hope, often finding solace in some unanticipated truth. Based out of Duluth, Minnesota, Death Valley Yacht Club is the creative collaboration of musicians Charlie Jacobs and Alex Oberton. The two-piece band’s signature sound features their intricate vocal harmonies sung over the interplay between their tightly-arranged acoustic guitars.

events.title: Shane Nelson - Havanas (Superior WI)
events.description: Cuban food and Live music with songwriter Shane Nelson Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. events.title: Max Subar
events.description: Max Subar and Minor Moon Fall Duo Tour. DM for address Chicago singer-songwriter Max Subar joins the Merge Records roster with his debut full-length album "Anything Could Be." Laid down on a mobile recording rig in a house on the shore of a frozen lake in Wisconsin, Max emerged after ten days of solitude with a record of neither fallow nor verdant earth, but, staggeringly, one that occupies the threshold between the two, a space that accommodates the potential for stagnation and growth: their hopes, their worries, the time it takes to arrive at an unknown destination, and the courage to accept what’s there, waiting to be realized. “There is so much room for newness in the weightiest or seemingly most paralyzing of times,” Subar explains. “No matter how foreign, frightening, anxiety-ridden, or unfamiliar chapters of life can feel, there is always an opportunity to tap deep into ourselves and land somewhere new, somewhere forward.”

events.description: house show, dm for address :: https://www.instagram.com/inclinestares/ Max Subar (duo) Minor Moon (duo) Kara Warren Minor Moon, The Light Up Waltz Out via Ruination Record Co., April 12th, 2024 At the heart of Minor Moon’s open-ended and knotty country rock songs is an undeniably inviting lightness. While the Chicago-based songwriter and bandleader Sam Cantor writes impressionistic songs about the end of the world, they’re wrapped in such a warm blanket of lush guitars and pastoral twang that they always leave a hopeful spark. On their latest LP, The Light Up Waltz, Cantor sings of the fantastical in magical traveling bands, swaying bridges, and aquamarine metamorphoses. Still, he’s concerned with fundamentally human questions about who we are and how we reinvent ourselves when everything crumbles around us. While the 2021 release of Minor Moon’s third LP Tethers coincided with a transitional period in Cantor’s life, The Light Up Waltz materialized during a time of unprecedented personal stability and creativity. He immersed himself in Chicago’s immensely collaborative music community performing live with V.V. Lightbody, Andrew Sa, Half Gringa, and more.

events.title: Zach Williams
events.description: Music is meant to feel “lived-in,” not unlike a favorite old jacket or a first car. At least that’s what multiplatinum two-time GRAMMY® Award-winning Arkansas-born and Nashville-based maverick Zach Williams would say. Through a fusion of southern rock spirit and country soul, Zach creates music with an exterior which is worn down in the best way, but all heart underneath rough guitar riffs and gravelly vocals. You’ll not only hear his journey in the music, but you’ll also see it in his unfiltered storytelling—how he went from a tiny town to international stardom, selling out shows, toppling charts, and collaborating with the likes of Dolly Parton. Along the way, he battled addiction, anxiety, and insecurity, coming out on the other side with a whole lot to say. After living through the lowest of lows and the highest of highs, he made a choice to trust his gut more than ever in 2021. Doing so had certainly served him well up to this point, so he wholeheartedly embraced his most formative inspirations, including rock and old school country.

events.title: Nu-Blu Bluegrass Artists
events.description: Nu-Blu, based in Siler City in central North Carolina, is comprised of Carolyn Routh, who handles bass and vocals; Austin Hefflefinger on vocals and banjo; Justin Harrison, on mandolin and fiddle; and Daniel Routh, who is the band’s Renaissance Man – guitarist, singer, manager, and tour coordinator, among many other roles. The group brings its lively and entertaining version of Americana-bluegrass music to audiences across the nation year-round. Their sound acknowledges the traditional institutions that have shaped it, yet is innovative and daring enough to bring a fresh sparkle to contemporary acoustic music that lands them squarely in the forefront of bands blazing the trail in acoustic entertainment. Influences range from the sounds of original bluegrass pioneers like Earl Scruggs, Jimmy Martin and Lester Flatt to rock bands of the 1980’s, and modern contemporary sounds such as Alison Krauss and Union Station. Carolyn’s soprano vocal approach might be described as similar to Ms. Krauss, except she carries a phrasing and emotional elegance that shows a clear originality.

events.title: Indecent Proposal
events.description: Sip & Serenade is back at Jack’s Place for a special edition night featuring Indecent Proposal’s lead guitarist, Jason Owen. Jason takes classic songs and flips them with his own twist — smooth grooves, sharp turns, and those little “wait... run that back” moments that catch the whole room at once. It’s the perfect kind of midweek reset: laid-back enough to hang, but the guitar work keeps you locked in. Bring your crew, grab a drink, and let Wednesday night get a little indecent. come out and get Indecent 😈😎🎸🤘💜 www.indyp218.com Indecent Proposal is a band out of Duluth, Minnesota, built around connection, feel, and songs that hold up in a room full of people. Blending modern alt-rock, groove-driven covers, and emotionally grounded originals, the band focuses on moments you can feel as much as hear. Their live shows move fluidly between intimacy and release—quiet verses, loud hearts, and choruses that come back at you from the crowd. Led by frontman Josh Brown, with Selie’s dynamic vocals, Jason Soderlund on guitar, Terry Beckman on bass, and Andy Fabian on drums, Indecent Proposal brings intention to every set and honesty to every song.

events.title: Ian Alexy
events.description: Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life. “Invokes 80s era Petty and Springsteen.” - Minneapolis Star Tribune “Stomping Blues Rock reminiscent of Dan Auerbach.”

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: After more than four decades together, 38 SPECIAL continues to bring their signature blast of Southern Rock to over 100 cities a year. And at each and every show, thousands of audience members are amazed by the explosive power of the band's performance. Their many Gold and Platinum album awards stand in testament to the endurance of a legendary powerhouse. With sales in excess of 20 million, most associate the band with their arena-rock pop smashes, “Hold On Loosely,” “Rockin’ Into the Night,” “Caught Up in You,” “Fantasy Girl,” “If I’d Been the One,” “Back Where You Belong,” “Chain Lightnin’,” “Second Chance,” and more – Timeless hits that remain a staple at radio, immediately recognizable from the first opening chord, and paving the way to their present-day touring regimen.

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: 38 Special is an American rock band. Formed by Guitarist/Vocalist Don Barnes and vocalist Donnie Van Zant in 1974 in Jacksonville, Florida, the band initially had a straight-ahead Southern rock sound, much like Lynyrd Skynyrd, the band of Donnie's older brother Ronnie. By the early 1980s, the band began incorporating elements of blues-rock and arena rock into their sound, kicking off a string of successful albums and singles. Among 38 Special's best-known songs are "Caught Up in You" (1982) and "If I'd Been the One" (1983), both of which hit #1 on Billboard magazine's album rock chart, and "Second Chance" (1989), a #1 hit on Billboard's adult contemporary chart. Their other hit singles include "Hold On Loosely" (1981) and "Back Where You Belong" (1984). The band is comprised of guitarist/vocalist Don Barnes, guitarist Jerry Riggs, bassist Barry Dunaway, keyboardist Bobby Capps, and drummer Gary Moffatt.

events.title: Teague Alexy
events.description: Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs. Teague’s first album of 2017, Circuit Sessions, combines multiple musical genres into a powerful new collection of Teague’s poetic songs with the lionstrong production and rhythm section of Eric Pollard (Actual Wolf) and Steve Garrington (Low) joined by Minneapolis guitarist Jake Hanson. Teague also has a new musical and storytelling podcast “Wisecracks & Roadside Flats.”
